ἀάατος.definition: in Il. ⏑–⏑⏑, not to be injured; in Od. ⏑–⏑⏑, 22.5, cf. 21.91, prob. unimpeachable, i.e. decisive

ἀαγής.definition: unbroken, hard, Od.11.575, Theoc.24.123, etc. . [First short ll. cc., long A.R.3.1251, Q.S.6.596.]

ἄαπτος.definition: not to be touched, resistless, invincible, Hom. , Hes.Op.148; Opp.H.5.629. in Hom.; cf

ἄατος.definition: contr. insatiate, c. gen., Hes.Th.714; Il.5.388; 22.218: abs., A.R.1.459. [First syll. short in Hes., long in A.R.]

ἀβαθής.definition: not deep, Arr.Tact.5.6; in; Geom., without depth, S.E.P.3.43, cf. Simp.in Ph.572.25

ἀβακίσκος.definition: Dim. of small stone for inlaying, in mosaic work, Moschio ap. Ath.5.207c

ἄβαξ.definition: reckoning-board, used for counting votes, Arist.Ath.69.1; board sprinkled with sand or dust for drawing geometrical diagrams, S.E.M.9.282, Iamb.Protr.34 , VP5.22

ἀβίαστος.definition: unforced, without force or; unstrained, unaffected, D.H.Dem.38

ἀβλής.definition: not thrown or shot, an arrow not yet used, Il.4.117; cf. A.R.3.279

ἀβόητος.definition: Dor. not loudly; not noised abroad, IG2.4174

ἀβόλλα.definition: = Lat. abolla, thick woollen cloak, Peripl.M.Rubr.6, CPR1.27

ἁβρότης.definition: splendour, luxury; of style, sweetness, charm, Hermog.Id.1.12

ἀγάθωμα.definition: embodiment of the good, Procl.in Prm.p.863S

ἀγαλλίς.definition: dwarf iris, Iris attica, h.Cer.7,426:—also Nic.Fr.74.31

ἄγαλμα.definition: pleasing gift, esp. for the gods, Od.8.509, of a bull adorned for sacrifice, ib.3.438; of a tripod, Hdt.5.60, al.; generally, = IG1.37312a, etc.; . . GDI5507 ; Simon.155; so, . . because sacred to her, E.Fr.968, = Ar.…

ἄγανος.definition: broken, sticks broken for firewood, S.Fr.231

ἀγάνωτος.definition: not enamelled or lacquered, Posidon.Medic. ap.Paul.Aeg.7.20, Zos.Alch.p.220B

ἀγασυλλίς.definition: the plant which produces Ferula marmarica, Dsc.3.84

ἄγγαρος.definition: in Persia, mounted courier, for carrying; term of abuse , Men.2 D., cf. Lib.Or.1.129

ἄγευστος.definition: Act., not tasting or having; Pass., tasteless, Arist.de An.422a30

ἄγη.definition: Dor. wonder, amazement; envy, malice, Hdt.6.61; of the gods, jealousy, A.Ag.131: pl. = Id.Fr.85

ἀγή.definition: fragment, splinter, A.Pers.425; E.Supp.693; place where the wave breaks, beach, A.R.1.554, Numen. ap.Ath.7.305a

ἀγήλατος.definition: driving out a curse, i. e. lightning which consumes and so purifies, Lyc.436

ἁγής.definition: guilty, accursed, dub. in Hippon.11; in good sense, pure, holy, of the sun, Emp.47

ἀγίγαρτος.definition: of grapes, etc., without seed or stone, Thphr.CP5.5.1, Aët.9.30

ἅγιος.definition: devoted to the gods; in good sense, sacred, holy

ἀγκάλη.definition: bent arm, mostly in pl; bend of knee, Cael.Aur.TP5.1.2

ἀγκών.definition: bend of the arm, hence, elbow; bend in animals' legs, X.Cyn.4.1

ἄγμα.definition: fragment, Plu.Phil.6; fracture; nasalized g, Ion ap.Prisc.Inst.1.39

ἀγμός.definition: fracture of a bone; broken cliff, crag, E.IT263; pl., Id.Ba.1094, Nic.Al.391, St.Byz. s.v

ἄγναπτος.definition: of cloth, not fulled or carded, hence; not cleansed, unwashed, ib.169c

ἁγνεών.definition: place of purity, for a brothel, Clearch.6

ἀγνώς.definition: of things, obscure, unintelligible, A.Ag.1051, cf. S.Ant.1001; dark, vague suspicion, Id.OT681

ἀγρός.definition: field, mostly in pl., fields, lands; country, opp. town, Od.17.182, E.Supp.884, etc.; Epich.169; in the country, Od.11.188; in the country, 1.190, 22.47; 1.185; in pl., 17.18; S.OT112; ib.1049; Id.El.313; Id.OT1051; T…

ἄγυιος.definition: without limbs, weak in limb, Hp.Mul.1.25

ἀγωγαῖος.definition: fit for leading by, of a dog's collar or leash, AP6.35

ἀγών.definition: Aeol. Alc.121 (also; place of contest, lists, course, Il.23.685, cf. 531, Od.8.260, Hes.Sc.312, Pi.P.9.114, and esp. Th.5.50: prov., out of the lists or course, i.e. beside the mark, Pi.P.1.44, Luc.Anach.21: pl., Od.8…

ἄγωνος.definition: = without angle, Thphr.HP7.6.2; Aeol. and Elean for q.v

ἄδαιτος.definition: of which none might eat, A.Ag.151

ἀδάρκη.definition: or salt efflorescence on the herbage of marshes, Dsc.5.119, Damocr. ap. Gal.13.105: Gal.12.370; Dim. ibid

ἀδευκής.definition: Hom. only in Od., 4.489; 10.245; 6.273, cf. A.R.2.267, etc. not sweet, i. e. bitter, cruel, or unexpected, cf. Apollon.Lex., expl. as not imitative, opp. Ael.NA5.38.)

ἀδήϊος.definition: contr. Dor. unmolested, unravaged, . . S.OC1533: of persons, not harmed, A.R.4.647

ἄδηκτος.definition: not gnawed or worm-eaten; metaph., unmolested, Phld.D.3Fr.81, Plu.2.864c. Adv. ib.448a

ἀδίαυλος.definition: with no way back, without return, of the nether world, E.Fr.868; . . Epigr.Gr.244.9

ἄδικος.definition: of persons, wrongdoing; obstinate, unmanageable, X.Cyr.2.2.26; the hard mouth of a horse, Id.Eq.3.5

ἀδίωκτος.definition: not to be eliminated, irremovable, Syn.Alch.p.63 B

ἄδωρος.definition: taking no gifts, incorruptible, c. gen; receiving no gifts, Max. Tyr.11.8

ἀδώτης.definition: non-giver, coined as antithesis of Hes.Op.355

ἀέθλιος.definition: gaining the prize, or running for it, a race-horse, Thgn.257; Call.Del.113:—contr. only in a restricted sense

ἄεμμα.definition: Ep. for bow-string or bow, Call.Dian.10, Ap.33

ἄζα.definition: heat, Opp.C.1.134, cf. 3.324; dryness, of the skin, Nic.Th.304

ἀζαλέος.definition: dry, parched, Il.20.491; metaph., harsh, cruel, AP5.237

ἄζεστος.definition: not coming to the boil, Hp.Morb.3.17

ἀζηλία.definition: simplicity of style, freedom from mannerisms, v.l. in Plu.Lyc.21

ἄζηλος.definition: unenvied, unenviable, dreary; Act., not envious, Menetor ap.Ath.13.594c

ἆζος.definition: contr. from a servant, Gloss. ap. Ath.6.267c

ἄζυγος.definition: unwedded, Luc.Am.44; = foreg., the vena azygos, Gal.15.529: in pl., not a pair, Str.6.1.8

ἄζυξ.definition: unyoked, unpaired; isolated, Arist.Pol.1253a7, cf. AP9.482.26 ; single, opp. Nonn.D.3.76: in pl., vowels, opp. ib.4.262

ἀζωΐα.definition: absence of life, Porph.Sent.21,23, Procl.in Prm.p.646 S., Olymp.in Grg.p.356 J

ἄζωνος.definition: confined to no zone or region, opp. local deities, Serv. ad Virg.Aen.12.118, cf. Dam.Pr.96,al

ἄζωος.definition: without life, Porph.Sent.20; without maggots, of seeds, Thphr.CP4.15.3

ἀθαλής.definition: or of the laurel, not verdant, withered, Plu.Pomp.31, Orac. ap. Ath.12.524b

ἀθαλπής.definition: without warmth, Nonn.D.37.151,40.286, etc. Adv. Hp.Acut.29

ἀθεησίη.definition: Ion. Subst. want of sight, blindness, Aret.CD1.4

ἄθεος.definition: without God, denying the gods, esp; abandoned of the gods, S.OT661; B.10.109

ἀθήητος.definition: Ion. for that may not be beheld, Nonn.D.5.305, al.; unseen, ib.2.6

ἀθήρ.definition: awn, Hes.Fr.117; barb of a weapon, A.Fr.154, Hp.Epid.5.49, Plu.Cat.Mi.70

ἀθηρία.definition: want of game, Ael.N.A.8.2; immunity from being hunted, ib.14.1

ἄθηρος.definition: without wild beasts or game; repelling noxious animals, Gp.10.32, etc

ἀθιγής.definition: untouched, Theopomp.Hist.76; of a; Act., not having touched, Porph. ap. Eus.PE5.10

ἀθλιβής.definition: not pressed or hurt, Nonn.D.9.31; not; Act., not pressing, ib.37.220

ἆθλος.definition: contr. from Ep. and Ion. which alone; = I, Theoc.8.11sqq.—On the proper difference of and v. II. .75.)

ἄθορος.definition: of male animals, veneris expers, Ant.Lib.13.7

ἀθροότης.definition: a being massed together, collectivity, opp. Epicur.Ep.2p.49U

ἄθυμος.definition: fainthearted, spiritless, once in Hom; without anger or passion, Pl.R.411b, Lg.888a

ἀθῷος.definition: —scot-free, E.Ba.672, etc; c. gen., free from a thing, Ar.Nu.1413; unpunished for offences, Lycurg.79, cf. D.S.14.76

ἀθώπευτος.definition: unflattered, without flattery; not open to flattery, Lyc.1399, cf. Nic.Dam.p.144 D

αἴγιλος.definition: a herb of which goats are fond, = I, Theoc.5.128, Babr.3.4

αἰγίλωψ.definition: poet. Nic.Th.857, haver-; Turkey oak, Quercus Cerris, Thphr.HP3.8.2

αἰγίς.definition: goatskin, worn as a dress, Hdt.4.189, E.Cyc.360 ; hence; esp. the skin shield of Zeus, Il.5.738, al.; lent by him to Athena, 2.447, al.; to Apollo, 15.318, al.; later, with fringe of snakes and Gorgon's head, the aegi…

αἴγλη.definition: the light of the sun or moon, Od.4.45; generally, radiance, gleam, Il.2.458; the gleam of her torches, S.OT207 ; of dying embers, E.Tr.549

αἰδήμων.definition: gen. bashful, modest; in bad sense, ignominious, shameful, Max.576

αἰδοῖον.definition: freq. in pl. privy parts; a sea animal, perh. pennatula, Nic.Fr.139, cf. Arist.HA532b23

αἰδοῖος.definition: having a claim to regard; Act., bashful, shamefaced, Od.17.578

αἰθάλη.definition: = esp. soot Hp.Mul.1.91; sublimed vapour, Zos.Alch.p.250B., al

αἰθής.definition: burning: the robe of Nessus, prov. of those who stir up Cratin.88, cf. Zen.1.33

αἶθος.definition: burning heat, fire, E.Rh.990, cf. Supp.208 codd. :—later also A.R.3.1304, Orph.L.174

αἴθρη.definition: Hom. and Ar. ll.cc.: later; air, as an element, Orac.Chald.169

αἴθυια.definition: diving-bird, prob. shearwater, Od.5.337, cf; metaph., ship, Lyc.230

αἷμα.definition: blood, Il.1.303, etc; of anything like blood, Tim.Fr.7; LXXSi.39.26, cf. App.Anth.3.166

αἱμάλωψ.definition: mass of blood: bloodshot place; as Adj., looking like clotted blood, Id.SD2.1

αἱματίς.definition: blood-redcloak, Arist.Col.797a6: perh. f.l. for sq

αἱμνίον.definition: basin for blood, v.l. for Od.3.444

αἵμων.definition: dub. sens., perh. eager; bloody, E.Hec.90, dub.l.in A.Supp.847

αἴνιγμα.definition: dark saying, riddle, Pi.Fr.177; taunt, Aristaenet.1.27

αἶνος.definition: poet. and Ion. word, tale, story; decree, resolution, IG4.926 ; opp. SIG672.15 , cf. EM36.16

αἴξ.definition: wild goat, prob. ibex , Od.14.50; Il.4.105; Od.9.155; 17.295:—proverbs, in Com. as a source of mysterious and suspected wealth, in allusion to the horn of Amalthea, Cratin.244; Com.Adesp.8; , of those who 'ask for tro…

αἶπος.definition: height, steep, A.Ag.285,309, etc.; to toil up-hill, Hp.Morb.2.51,70; metaph. of a difficult task, E.Alc.500: hence i.e. the weariness of the ascent , Id.Ph.851

ἄιρος.definition: only in phrase Irus, unhappy Irus, Od.18.73

αἴσακος.definition: branch of myrtle or laurel, handed by one

αἴσιμος.definition: also Od.23.14: :—Ep. Adj; agreeable to the decree of fate, meet, fitting, Od.22.46; opp. 2.231; right-minded, 23.14; to drink in decent measure, 21.294

αἴσιος.definition: meet, right, Lat. justum pondus, Nic.Th.93; Just.Edict.13.4.1

ἄϊστος.definition: —poet. Adj. unseen; Act., unconscious of, E.Tr.1314, cf. 1321

αἶσχος.definition: shame, disgrace, Hom. (freq. in pl; in pl., disgraceful deeds, Od.1.229

αἰών.definition: Ion. and Ep. also as in Pi.P.4.186; one's life, destiny, lot, S.Tr.34, E.Andr.1215, Fr.30, etc

αἰώρα.definition: swing, hammock, chariot on springs; noose, halter, S.OT1264

ἄκαιρος.definition: ill-timed, unseasonable; of persons, importunate, troublesome, Thphr.Char.12; Alciphr.3.62

ἀκακαλίς.definition: gall of the Oriental tamarisk; = Eumach. ap. Ath.15.681e

ἀκακία.definition: shittah tree, Acacia arabica, Dsc.1.101; = Genista acanthoclada. Dsc. l.c

ἄκανθος.definition: bearsfoot, Acanthus mollis, a plant; Acanthus, = Virg.G.2.119

ἀκάρδιος.definition: wanting the heart, Polyaen.8.23.33; of wood, without heart or pith, solid, Thphr.HP3.12.1

ἀκαρί.definition: kind of mite, bred in wax, Arist.HA557b8

ἄκαυλος.definition: without stalk, Dsc.1.8.2; of a feather, without shaft or stalk, Arist.PA682b18

ἀκέανος.definition: kind of leguminous vegetable, Pherecr.188, cf. Ael.Dion.Fr.28

ἀκέλυφος.definition: without husk or capsule, of fruits, Thphr.CP1.17.8

ἀκήριος.definition: unharmed by the generally; having no i.e. with no fortune attached to them, Hes.Op.823

ἀκιδοειδής.definition: barb-like, of quadrilateral with re- entrant angle, Procl.in Euc.p.165 F

ἄκινος.definition: wild basil, Calamintha graveolens, Dsc.3.43:—also ib

ἀκίς.definition: pointed object; hence; barb of an arrow or hook, Plu.Demetr.20; AP6.5

ἀκίχητος.definition: not to be reached, unattainable; not to be reached by prayer, inexorable, A.Pr.186

ἀκκώ.definition: bogey, that nurses used to frighten children with, Plu.2.1040b: acc. to others, vain woman, Zen.1.53

ἄκλιτος.definition: Gramm., indeclinable, D.T.641.23; Math., = Procl.in Euc.p.290F

ἄκλονος.definition: of the pulse, steady, regular, Gal.9.347; of a limb, free from jars, 17.513; of a rider, with a firm seat, Palaeph.52

ἀκμάδιον.definition: kind of surgical instrument, Hermes 38.281 ; conical crucible, Ps.-Mos.Alch.p.39B

ἄκμητος.definition: Lyr. S.Ant.609 Jebb, =; not causing pain, Nic.Th.737

ἄκνημος.definition: without calf, of the leg, Plu.2.520c

ἄκνισος.definition: without fat of sacrifices; lacking in fats, Thphr.CP2.4.6, cf. Plu.2.123b

ἄκολπος.definition: without sinus genitalis, of the pipe-fish, Ael.NA15.16

ἀκόμμωτος.definition: unpainted; metaph., without meretricious ornament, Them.Or.18.218b

ἀκόνιον.definition: in Medicine, specific for eyes, prob. powdered by rubbing on an Dsc.1.98

ἀκόνιτον.definition: leopard's bane, Aconitum Anthora; wolf's bane, Aconitum Napellus, Dsc.4.77

ἀκόνιτος.definition: without dust, combat or; f.l. for Dsc.1.7; for Arist.GA739b12

ἄκος.definition: cure, remedy, c. gen. rei; means of obtaining a thing, c. gen., E.Hel.1055

ἄκρα.definition: Ion. highest or farthest; hill-top, height, Od.8.508, Hymn.Is.72

ἀκρασία.definition: Ion. bad mixture, ill temperature, opp. an unwholesome climate, Thphr.CP3.2.5; of meats, Hp.VM7; ib.18

ἀκταία.definition: a Persian state robe, Democr.Ephes.1; marble mortar, Clearch.65; cf

ἀκτή.definition: headland, foreland, promontory; generally, tract of land running out into the sea, of the north and south coasts of Asia Minor, Hdt.4.38; of Africa, as jatting out from Asia, 4.41, cf. 177; of Cape Sepias, 7.183, al.;…

ἄκτιος.definition: of the sea-shore, of Pan as god of the coast, Theoc.5.14; of Apollo, A.R.1.404

ἀκτίς.definition: metaph., brightness, splendour, glory, Pi.P.11.48, I.4.42; splendid fortunes, Id.P.4.255

ἀκύκλιος.definition: one who has not gone the round of studies, opp. Pl.Com.227

ἀκύλιστος.definition: not to be rolled about: metaph; of Protagoras, not without volubility or versatility, Id.5

ἀκωκή.definition: scorpion's sting, Orph.L.622; snake's fangs, ib.126

ἁλάδρομος.definition: dithyrambic word coined by Ar.Av.1396, prob. from , race over the sea

ἀλαλητός.definition: generally, loud shouting, Il.2.149; halloo, in hunting, Nic.Dam.p.6 D

ἀλέα.definition: Ion. avoiding, escape, . . Il.22.301 ; Hp.Aër.19: c.gen., shelter from a thing, Hes.Op.545.—Ep.and Ion. word

ἄλειφαρ.definition: unguent, anointing-oil; pitch or resin, to seal wine-jars, Theoc.7.147.—Cf. foreg

ἄλευρον.definition: mostly in pl. =; generally, meal, Dsc.1.72; 3.40, cf. 2.102; made trom dried sorbs, 1.120

ἀλεωρή.definition: Att. escape, Il.24.216; place of shelter, Opp.H.1.790

ἄλη.definition: wandering or roaming without home or hope; wandering of mind, distraction, E.Med.1285

ἀλήιος.definition: without corn-lands, poor in lands, or without booty, opp. Il.9.125, 267

ἄληπτος.definition: not to be laid hold of, hard to catch; incomprehensible, Phld.Mus.p.54K., Plu.Nic.11, al

ἄλησις.definition: = of the course of the; grinding, Gp.9.19.7

ἀλητός.definition: poet. for was sold to grind in the mill, Babr.29.1; Adj.ground, Archig. ap. Orib.8.1.33

ἁλία.definition: Ion. assembly of people, in; generally, meeting, assembly, Hdt.5.29,79; of the Persians, 1.125

ἁλιάδης.definition: Dor. for religious association at Rhodes, IG12.155

ἁλιάς.definition: of or belonging to sea: , fishing-boat or bark, Arist.HA533b20, Moschio ap.Ath.5.208f, D.S.3.21

ἀλίβας.definition: dead body, corpse; dead river, i.e. Styx, S.Fr.790

ἅλιμος.definition: of or belonging to the sea; as Subst., tree purslane, Atriples Halimus, Antiph.160, Thphr.HP4.16.5, Dsc.1.91

ἄλινος.definition: without net, game not caught with net, AP9.244

ἄλιξ.definition: groats of rice-wheat; = Lat. hallec, fish-sauce, Dsc.4.148, Gp.20.46.2

ἀλιπής.definition: without fat meagre, poor, Hices; unfailing, Poet. ap. Porph.Antr.8

ἀλλᾶς.definition: force-meat, sausage or black-pudding, Hippon.48, Ar.Eq.161, Crates Com.17, etc

ἄλλιξ.definition: man's upper garment, Euph.144, Call.Fr149 ; purple cloak , EM68.33

ἄλλιτος.definition: = foreg., Epic.Alex.Adesp.6.5; shrieking unanswered prayers, App.Anth.4.54.7

ἀλλοινία.definition: drinking several wines, mixing liquors, Plu.2.661c

ἀλλοῖος.definition: of another sort or kind; containing or subject to diversity, Porph.Sent.20,21

ἅλμα.definition: spring, leap, poet.for Prose; jumping, asanathletic contest, Simon.153:—in pl., jumping-ground, BCH23.566

ἁλμυρίς.definition: anything salt, and so; salt humour, Hp.Epid.3.13; salt scum, Arist.Mete.357b4

ἄλοβος.definition: with lobe wanting, of livers of victims, X.HG3.4.15, Plu.Ages.9, Arr.An.7.18.4

ἄλογος.definition: speechless, Pl.Lg.696e. Adv. without speech, S.OC131, = Lat. dies nefastus, on which no business may be done, Luc.Lex.9

ἀλόχευτος.definition: born not in the natural way, of Athena; unborn, Nonn.D.8.27

ἄλοχος.definition: poet., partner of; unwedded, of Artemis, Pl.Tht.149b, cf. Porph.ad Il.11.155

ἅλσις.definition: leaping, Hp.Morb.Sacr.17, Arist.EN1174a31, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.31.5, etc

ἄλσις.definition: growth, Did. ad D.13.32, Apollon.Lex. s.v. etc

ἀλύη.definition: socket for q.v., Eratosth. ap. EM173.24; dub. l. Phld.Mort.p.318M

ἅλυσις.definition: collectively, chains, bondage, Plb.21.3.3; link in chain armour, Arr.Tact.3.5

ἄλυσσον.definition: madwort, Farsetia clypeata; Galen's madwort, Sideritis romana, Ruf.Fr.76.10; cf. sq

ἄλυσσος.definition: curing madness, Asclep. ap. Gal.14.168; well curing hydrophobia, Paus.8.19.3

ἀλφάριον.definition: Dim. of plumb-line, level, Theo Sm.in Ptol.p.228 H

ἀλωεύς.definition: Ep. one who works in an husbandman, A.R.3.1401, Arat.1045, etc.: in Hom. only as pr. n

ἀλωή.definition: more commonly, any prepared ground , garden, orchard, vineyard, etc., Il.5.90, Od.6.293, etc.: i.e. sea, Opp.H.1.797

ἁλώνητος.definition: bought with salt, worthless slaves from Thrace, because Thracians sold men for salt, Zen.2.12

ἁμαδέον.definition: kind of fig, Cretan, Hermonax. ap. Ath.3.76f

ἀμάρα.definition: Ion. trench, conduit, channel; hollow of ear, EM77.23

ἁμάσυκον.definition: with or without fruit-tree flowering at the same time as the fig, Paus.Gr.Fr.42

ἄμβη.definition: Ion. for raised edge or protuberance, Hp.Art.7, cf. 80, Gal.18.340; rim of felloe of wheel, Democr.29

ἄμβιξ.definition: spouted cup, Ath.11.480d:—also; cap of still, Dsc.5.95

ἀμείωτος.definition: not to be diminished, Ph.2.66; incapable of diminution, Simp.in Cael.109.22. Adv. Olymp.in Alc.p.111C

ἄμεσος.definition: immediate: of propositions that cannot be proved syllogistically by means of a middle term, Arist.APr.68b30, APo.72b19, etc.; direct opposites, Plot.6.3.20. Adv. immediately, Olymp.in Phlb.p.256 S., Alex.Aphr.in Metap…

ἄμης.definition: kind of milk cake, Ar.Pl.999, Antiph.89; kind of oven, Dieuch.ap Orib.4.5.2

ἄμικτος.definition: unmingled, that will not mingle, Emp.35.8; unmixed, pure, ib.50e, unmixed with a thing, Id.Plt.310d; of poems, uniform in metre e.g. of the Epic hexameter, Heph.Poëm.2

ἀμιξία.definition: Ion. a being and so; purity, Thphr.CP4.16.2

ἄμιτρος.definition: without head-band or girdle, girls who have not yet put on the woman's girdle, i.e. unmarriageable, Call.Dian.14

ἅμμα.definition: anything tied or made to tie; noose, halter, E.Hipp.781

ἀμμορία.definition: Ion. poet. for , what is man's fate and what is not, or their good fortune and their bad, Od.20.76, cf. AP9.284

ἄμμορος.definition: poet. for , without share; later, simply, free from, without, Q.S.1.430

ἀμνή.definition: Dor. fem. of ewe-lamb, GDI3639 , 4990.11 , Orph.A.319

ἀμνήμων.definition: Dor. gen. unmindful; Pass., forgotten, not mentioned, E.Ph.64

ἀμνίον.definition: bowl in which the; inner membrane round the foetus, Emp.71; cf

ἄμομφος.definition: Act., having nothing to complain of, cj. Robortellus for ib.413

ἀμοργός.definition: one who squeezes or drains; lanterns which protect [the light] from winds, Emp.p.84

ἄμορος.definition: = c. gen., E.Med.1395; abs., unlucky, wretched, cj. Pors. for in S.OT248

ἄμυνα.definition: warding off an attack, self-defence; vengeance, requital, Ps.-Phoc.77, Phld.Ir.p.66 W., Nic.Dam.p.104D., Plot.4.4.17, etc

ἄμυος.definition: not showing muscle, Hp.Art.52, cf. Orib.Syn.5.44.20

ἀμύριστος.definition: not steeped in unguents; metaph., rude, rough, Heraclit.92

ἄμυρος.definition: watery, S.Fr.512, but perh. not perfumed, of byres

ἄμφαυξις.definition: callus or overgrowth on the scar of a removed branch , Thphr.HP3.7.1

ἀμφίαλος.definition: = foreg., freq. of Ithaca in Od., as; living amid seas, Plu.2.667e

ἀμφίας.definition: a bad Sicilian wine, Nicostr.Com.18, Sosicr.Com.7; cf

ἀμφίθυρος.definition: with a door on both sides, with double; Subst. hall, Theoc.14.42

ἀμφίλοξος.definition: slanting both ways, utter ambiguous oracles, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.5, cf. 16

ἀμφίπολις.definition: poet. encompassing city; Subst. city encompassed by a river, as pr. n., Th.4.102, etc

ἀμφίπυρος.definition: with fire at each end, of the; with fire all round, Id.Aj.1405

ἀμφίσκιος.definition: throwing shadow both ways; shady all round, Opp.H.1.789

ἀμφούριον.definition: acknowledgement paid to neighbours on sale of a plot of land, PHal.1.253

ἀμφώβολος.definition: javelin or spit with double; as Adj., in neut. pl., roasted on the spit, of victims sacrificed in divination, S.Fr.1006

ἀμωμίς.definition: plant used for adulterating amomum, Dsc.1.15, cf. Plin.HN12.49, Edict.Diocl.Troez.21

ἄμωμον.definition: Indian spice-plant, prob. Nepaul cardamom, Amomum subulatum, Arist.Fr.110, Thphr.HP9.7.2, Dsc.1.15

ἄνα.definition: voc. of king, only in the phrases contr. and and always as address to gods: fem., = Pi.P.12.3: ult. elided only in h.Ap.526 codd.—Ep., Lyr., and occasionally Trag., as S.OC1485

ἀνάβασις.definition: concrete, = all the horsemen, S.OC1070; ascension, Ascens.Is.10.21

ἀναγρία.definition: time when hunting was forbidden, close season, X.Cyn.5.34

ἀνάδηξις.definition: lit. biting: hence in Thphr.CP3.17.5 of the stimulating effect of certain manures

ἀνάεδνος.definition: without bride-price, Il.9.146, 13.366; also of the husband, bringing no gifts, Nonn.D.4.43, 48.633

ἀναιδής.definition: shameless, of Agamemnon; c. gen., ruthless in havoc, Il.5.593

ἄναιμος.definition: opp. bloodless, of parts; of animals, Id.PA678a33, al

ἀνάκανθος.definition: without a spine, of certain fish; of plants, without thorns, Thphr.HP3.12.9

ἀναλδής.definition: not thriving, feeble, Hp.Aër.15; barren, Ar.V.1045 ; without fruiting, Arat.333

ἀνάλογος.definition: according to a due proportionate; well-proportioned, suitable, Philostr.Im.1.10

ἄναλος.definition: without salt, not salted; of salt itself, salt which is no salt, Ev. Marc.9.50:2

ἄναμμα.definition: ignited mass, Epicur.Ep.1p.28U. ; of the sun, Heraclit. ap.Placit.2.20.16, cf. Zeno Stoic.1.35, Cleanth.ib.112

ἀνάνετος.definition: not relaxed, Stoic.2.129, cf. 3.141; not capable of diminution, Porph.Intr.20.4

ἄναντος.definition: not winnowed or bruised, dub. in S.Fr.294

ἀναξία.definition: command, behest; lack of value: inferiority, Pl.Prt.356a

ἀναπλοκή.definition: in Music, progression of notes ascending in the scale, opp. Ptol.Harm.2.12

ἀνάπλοος.definition: contr. sailing up-; putting out to sea, Plb.1.53.13, etc

ἄναρμος.definition: without joints, of atoms, Gal.1.416, cf; loose, of the groin, prob. l. in Philostr.Gym.48

ἀνάρτιος.definition: uneven, odd, Pl.Phd.104e, al; at odds with one, hostile, Plu.2.1030a

ἀναστολή.definition: putting back, Plu.Pomp.2; opening up of a fistula, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.23.60

ἄναυλος.definition: without the flute, a; unskilled in flute-playing, Luc.Halc.7

ἄναυς.definition: gen. only A.Pers.680 in nom. pl., ships that are ships no more

ἀναφής.definition: impalpable, Pl.Phdr.247c; of wine, tasteless, insipid, Plu.2.650b

ἀναφυγή.definition: escape, release from; place of retreat, Plu.Aem.16

ἄνδηρον.definition: raised bank by the side of a river or; border, edge, of the sea, dub. in B.1.54 ; Opp.H.4.319

ἀνδρεία.definition: Ion. , generally written; in bad sense, hardihood, insolence, D.Chr.12.13

ἀνέλυτρος.definition: unsharded, of bees, wasps, etc., opp. , Arist.HA490a15,532a24, al

ἀνέμητος.definition: not distributed, Aeschin.1.102; Act., having no share, Plu.Cat.Mi.26

ἀνερευθής.definition: of cancerous ulcers, pallid, Archig. ap. Aët.16.106 , but prob. f.l. for

ἀνήλατος.definition: not malleable, Arist.Mete.385a16; not struck with a hammer, LXXJb.41.15

ἀνήρ.definition: voc. pl. Aeol. dat. pl. Alc.Supp.14.8: late nom. sg. Cat.Cod.Astr.7.109.7: in Att. the Art. often forms a crasis with the Noun, for for etc., for the Ion. crasis is Hdt.4.161,134: Ep. also dual pl. [Ep. Poets mostly u…

ἀνθέλιξ.definition: the interior curvature of the ear, the exterior being Ruf.Onom.44

ἄνθη.definition: full bloom of a flower or plant; blossom or bloom, Nic.Th.625, Ael.NA12.4

ἄνθρωπος.definition: Att. crasis Ion. for; in pl., mankind, . . Il.9.134; . . S.Ph.306; depart this life, Paus.4.26.5, cf. Philostr.VA8.31

ἀνθυλλίς.definition: a plant, Cressa cretica, Dsc.3.136; herb ivie, Ajuga Iva, ibid., Plin.HN26.84

ἀνία.definition: Ion. Aeol. grief, sorrow; concrete, the killjoy of our feast, Od.17.446; inevitable bane, of Scylla, 12.223; an annoyance, 15.394. [In Hom. and S. always also E.IT1031 . Other Poets made the long or short as the verse…

ἀνίκανος.definition: insufficient, incapable, Babr.92; dissatisfied with everything, Arr.Epict.4.1.106

ἀνικία.definition: non-victory, Pythag. term, f.l. for Arist.Metaph.990a24, cf. Alex.Aphr.ad loc

ἄνοδος.definition: having no way or road, impassable, E.IT889 ; opp. X.An.4.8.10

ἄνοζος.definition: with no, or very few, branches, Thphr.HP1.8.1, etc.: Comp. ib.3.13.3:—also ib.1.5.4, al

ἄνομος.definition: lawless, impious, Hdt.1.162; of; c. gen., i.e. without Law and therefore without God, 1 Ep.Cor.9.21. Adv. = Ep.Rom.2.12

ἀνόνητος.definition: Dor. unprofitable; Act., c. gen., deprive of all benefit from . ., D.18.141, cf. 19.315, Plu.2.800d, Nic.Dam.p.13D

ἀνόξυντος.definition: not to be written with the acute accent, Eust.930.57

ἄνορχος.definition: without testicles, i.e. castrated; without stones, Arist.Fr.267

ἄνοσος.definition: Ion. and Ep. without sickness; c. gen., untouched by ill, E.IA982; Arist.HA604a12,22

ἀνούσιος.definition: without substance; in Alchemy, not affecting substance, superficial in action, Zos.Alch.p.160 B.,al

ἀνοψία.definition: want of fish to eat with bread

ἀντάξιος.definition: also Theoc.17.114:—worth just; abs., worth as much, worth no less, Il.1.136

ἀντέρως.definition: return-love, love-for-love; Anteros, personified as a god who avenged slighted love, Paus.1.30.1, etc.:—but also a god who struggled against Id.6.23.5

ἀντήνωρ.definition: instead of a man, dust for men, A.Ag.442.—In Il. as pr. n

ἀντιάς.definition: tonsil, mostly in pl., Hp.Morb.2.11 and 30: esp. when inflamed, Cels.7.12, Gal.7.263; cf

ἀντίδορος.definition: instead of skin, with a green husk as integument, AP6.22

ἀντίθεος.definition: equal to the gods, godlike (cf; contrary to God, Ph.1.566, al

ἀντιλέων.definition: lion-like, formed like Ar.Eq.1044; where, however, it is in fact a pr. n

ἀντίλυρος.definition: responsive to the lyre or like that of the lyre , of the flute, S.Tr.643

ἀντίπαις.definition: like a child, A.Eu.38; instead of a boy, i.e. no longer a boy, S.Fr.564

ἀντίπηξ.definition: wheeled cradle or perambulator for infants, E.Ion19; ib.40

ἀντιπλάδη.definition: substance or process for protecting walls from damp, Ath.Mitt.26.110

ἀντίπλοια.definition: sailing close to the wind: metaph. of a mixed constitution, dub. l. in Plb.6.10.7

ἀντίσιγμα.definition: sigma reversed, as a critical; symbol for ps, Priscian.Inst.1.42

ἀντισφήν.definition: counter-wedge which drives out another, Ph.Bel.67.32

ἀντίτομος.definition: cut as a remedy for an; having opposite curvatures for cutting, Paul.Aeg.6.30

ἀντίφραξις.definition: Pythag. name for seventeenth day of the month, ib.367f

ἀντίφρασις.definition: Rhet. and Gramm; expression by means of negation, Anon.Fig.p.212S

ἄντορος.definition: dialectic form of opposite boundary, counterfence, Tab.Heracl.1.60, al

ἄντρον.definition: poet. word, cave, Hom. only in Od., as; inner chamber, closet, LXX3 Ki.16.18

ἄντυξ.definition: edge or rim of anything round or; rim of round shield, 11.6.118, al., E.Rh.373

ἀνώχυρος.definition: = not fortified, X.Ages.6.6; open, clear, f.l.for Hp.Aër.24

ἄξαλλα.definition: a herb found on the Euphrates and used as a remedy for fever, Chryserm. ap. Ps.-Plu.Fluv.20.3

ἄοζος.definition: = servant, attendant, esp. belonging to a temple, A.Ag.231 , cf. Call.Del.249, IG9.976

ἀπαγωγή.definition: leading away, of troops, X.An.7.6.5; leading into captivity, LXXIs.10.4, al

ἀπαθής.definition: not suffering or having suffered, c. gen; Medic., of organs, unaffected, sound, Aret.SD1.7, cf. Gal.5.122; good eggs, Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.76

ἄπαις.definition: children of Night, yet children none, dub. l. in A.Eu.1034

ἀπάλαμος.definition: = foreg., helpless, Hes.Op.20; of Tantalus, Pi.O.1.59. metri gr., Hes.l.c.]

ἀπαλοιφή.definition: effacing, expunging, Gloss; prob.l. for , paste, amalgam, Zos.Alch.p.222B. [Perh. cf

ἀπαμοιβή.definition: alternation: masonry laid in courses of headers and stretchers, IG2.1054c60

ἀπάπη.definition: dandelion, Taraxacum officinale, Thphr.HP7.7.1, 7.8.3 and 11.3 , cf. Plin.HN21.99

ἄπαππος.definition: with no grandfather: metaph., light not unfathered by the Idaean flame, A.Ag.311

ἄπαρνος.definition: denying utterly; Pass., denied, . . to whom nothing is denied, A.Supp.1039

ἀπαρτία.definition: Ion. = household; spoil, including captives, ib.Nu.31.17,18

ἀπαρχή.definition: beginning of a sacrifice, primal offering , E.Or.96, cf. Ph.1525 ; later, a banquet held on this occasion, Plu.2.40b

ἀπάτητος.definition: untrodden, AP6.51; not trodden down: hence metaph., unusual, Democr.131

ἄπειρος.definition: without trial or experience of; boundless, infinite

ἀπειρωδίν.definition: knowing not the pains of child- birth, Nonn.D.16.152

ἄπεκτος.definition: lit. uncombed: hence, unshorn, of sheep less than a year old, Androt.41, cf. Philoch.64

ἄπεπλος.definition: unrobed, i.e. in her tunic only, of a girl, Pi.N.1.50; i.e. clad in black, E.Ph.324

ἀπέραντος.definition: boundless, infinite, of space; allowing no escape, whence none can pass, A.Pr.153,1087

ἀπέρασις.definition: spitting out, vomiting; carrying off of moisture, Thphr.CP2.9.8: metaph., Iamb.Myst.3.9

ἀπέρωτος.definition: loveless, unloving, like read by M2 in A.Ch.600; but v. foreg

ἄπηκτος.definition: not capable of being solidified; not solid, Sor.1.47

ἀπήνη.definition: four-wheeled wagon, drawn by mules; later, any car or chariot, A.Ag.906, S.OT753; ib.803; war-chariot, Str.4.5.2; cf

ἀπηνής.definition: Ep. Adj. ungentle, rough, hard, of persons; in physical sense, hard, Aret.SD1.14, cf. 2.12; unpleasant to taste, CA1.5

ἀπηξία.definition: want of solidity, liability to flux, Ptol.Tetr.204; incapacity for solidification, Ar.Byz.Epit.15.9

ἀπήορος.definition: Dor. hanging on high, far distant, Arat.396: c. gen., aloof from them, Pi.P.8.86

ἀπιᾶτον.definition: wine flavoured with celery, Gp.8.30, Alex.Trall.10

ἀπίθανος.definition: incredible, unlikely, Pl.Lg.663e; of persons, not to be trusted or relied on, in a matter, Aeschin.2.3

ἀπιθής.definition: poet. for I, AP5.86 ; for II, lacking in persuasion, Timo26

ἀπίλητος.definition: not to be pressed close, i.e. either incompressible or elastic, Arist.Mete.385a17,387a16

ἀπίων.definition: gen. not fat, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.4.120e, Aret.CD1.5

ἀπληγής.definition: of verses, free from metrical defect, Diom.p.498 K

ἄπληγος.definition: not smitten with disease, etc., PMag.Par.1.1063

ἄπληκτος.definition: unstricken, of a horse needing no whip or; Act., not striking, in Adv. without pulsation, Procl.in Cra.p.37P

ἄπνοος.definition: contr. wind, with but; unventilated, Plu.2.515b; air-tight, Herod.8.74

ἀποβώμιος.definition: far from an altar, godless; in Eust.1720.28, literally, not offered on an altar, but on the ground

ἀπογώνιον.definition: = Vett.Val.349.22: in pl., tables of such degrees for calculating expectation of life, Critodem.ibid., cf. 304.21

ἀποδορά.definition: peeling of the skin, Agathin. ap. Orib.10.7.18

ἄποδος.definition: = not having the use of one's feet, Tab. Defix. Aud.159A44

ἄποικος.definition: away from home, abroad; mostly as Subst

ἄποιος.definition: without quality or attribute; inert, Procl.Inst.80, cf. eund.in Ti.3.337 D

ἀπόκλητος.definition: called or chosen out, select; in the Aetolian League, members of the select council, Plb.20.1.1, etc

ἀπόκροτος.definition: beaten or trodden hard; of style, sonorous, Anon.in Rh.191.20, 225.11

ἀπόλυμα.definition: filth, Harp.s.v. in pl., fragments of tissue, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.10.13, Gal.19.422

ἀπόνευσις.definition: bending or turning off, Stoic.2.289; dissent, opp. Anon.Fig.p.179S

ἀπόνηρος.definition: not vicious, harmless; Medic., not malignant, Antyll. ap. Orib.5.29.8

ἀπόνητος.definition: without toil or trouble. Adv., Sup; without suffering, S.El.1065

ἀπόρευτος.definition: that cannot or may not be travelled; not to be traversed, Ph.2.112,al

ἀπορία.definition: Ion. being hence; of places, difficulty of passing, X.An.5.6.10

ἄποτος.definition: not drinkable, Hdt.4.81; not drunk from, Philostr.VA4.20

ἄπουρος.definition: far from the boundaries, v.l. in S.OT194

ἀποφράς.definition: not to be mentioned; rarely as masc. Adj., impious, wicked, Eup.309; Luc.Pseudol.32

ἄποψις.definition: lofty spot or tower which commands a view, belvedere, Str.17.1.16, Plu.Comp. Cim.Luc.1

ἀπραξία.definition: rest from business, leisure, Men.633: in pl., = Lat. justitium, Plu.Sull.8

ἀπρίωτος.definition: in Surgery, without the use of the trepan, Hp.VC14; not trephined, ib.20

ἀπρόβατος.definition: making no progress, of persons; not advancing matters, inconclusive, Id.Sign.6 and 35

ἀπροξίς.definition: burning bush, Dictamnus albus, Pythag. ap. Plin. HN24.158

ἀπρόσωπος.definition: without a face, i.e. without beauty of; without a mask, undisguised, Aristid.1.409 J

ἄπτερος.definition: without wings, unwinged, Hom. only in Od; opp. without wings, of insects, Arist.HA523b17; Id.PA642b33

ἀπτώς.definition: not falling or liable to fall, of a wrestler's art, Pi.O.9.92; Pl.R.534c; M.Ant.7.61; Plu.Comp.Arist.Cat.2

ἀπυρεξία.definition: absence of fever, time or state free from fever, Gal.17.69, cf. 19.399

ἀπύρηνος.definition: without stone or kernel, pipless; with no spine, Archestr.Fr.8 codd

ἀπφῦς.definition: gen. a term of endearment used by children to their father, papa, Theoc.15.14:— Eust. expld. as

ἄραβος.definition: gnashing or chattering of teeth; generally, rattling, ringing, Call.Del.147

ἄρακος.definition: a leguminous plant, wild chickling; neut., a variety which grew as a weed among lentils, Thphr.HP8.8.3

ἀρακώδης.definition: like tine- tare, Lathyrus tuberosus, Thphr.HP1.6.12

ἀράξα.definition: fabulous plant which grows by the Araxes, Ps.-Plu.Fluv.23.2

ἄραξις.definition: dashing, beating, Cass.Pr.25; kind of bread used in Athamania, Ath.3.114b

ἄργμα.definition: only in pl. = firstlings at a sacrifice or feast, Od.14.446

ἀρδιοθήρα.definition: forceps to extract arrow- heads, etc., Serv. ad Virg.Aen.8.453, 12.404

ἄρδις.definition: point of an arrow, acc. Hdt.4.81

ἀρειά.definition: Ion. and poet. collective noun, menaces, threats, . . Il.20.109, but . . 21.339; . . 17.431

ἀρείων.definition: gen. used as Comp. of; a kind of snail or slug, Ael.NA10.5

ἀρημένος.definition: pf. part. Pass., expld. by Gramm. by distressed, worn out, once in Il., 18.435; more freq. in Od., 6.2; 9.403; 11.136; 18.53. [Prob. akin to

ἄρηξις.definition: help, succour, from; c. gen. rei, help against a thing, means of averting it, S.El.876

ἀριθμός.definition: number, first in Od; amount, sum, Aeschin.1.78; X.An.2.2.6; a sum of money, Id.Cyr.8.2.16

ἀρκάνη.definition: bar to which the threads of the warp are fastened, Id

ἄρμα.definition: that which one takes: food; burden, load, Aq.De.1.12, al

ἁρμή.definition: junction, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.154 ; fitting together, of shields, Q.S.11.361; suture of a wound, Hp. ap.Erot.; of the skull-bones, Id. ap. Gal.19.86

ἁρμός.definition: joint, in masonry, IG1.322; in; bolt, peg, E.Fr.360.12

ἀρναβώ.definition: zedoary, Posidon. Jun. ap. Paul.Aeg.7.3:—also Aët.7.135

ἀρνηάς.definition: prob. some sort of sheep, Schwyzer644.15

ἀρνίον.definition: Dim. of a little lamb, Lys.32.21; sheepskin, fleece, Luc.Salt.43

ἄρον.definition: cuckoo-pint, Arum italicum, Arist.HA600b11; Egyptian arum, Colocasia antiquorum, Plin.HN19.96, Gal.6.650

ἀρρεψία.definition: equilibrium of the soul, absence of bias, D.L.9.74, S.E.P.1.190, etc

ἄρρις.definition: without power of scenting; noseless, Str.2.1.9

ἀρρώξ.definition: without cleft or breach, unbroken, S.Ant.251: also c. Subst. neut., like Id.Fr.156

ἄρσις.definition: raising or lifting; distillation, Ps.-Democr. ap.Zos.Alch.p.152 B.; sublimation, ibid

ἀρτάνη.definition: that by which something is hung up, rope, noose, halter, A.Ag.875,1091 , etc.; S.OT1266; Id.Ant.54

ἄρτημα.definition: hanging ornament, ear-ring; cord for suspension, e. g. of the steelyard, Arist.Mech.853a34, b25, IG2.834c13, al.; Str.1.1.20

ἀρτήρ.definition: a kind of felt shoe, Pherecr.38; that by which anything is carried, LXXNe.4.17

ἀρτιότης.definition: soundness, entireness; of numbers, evenness, opp. Arist.Metaph.1004b11

ἄρτος.definition: cake or loaf of wheat-bread, mostly in pl

ἀρχός.definition: = dux Orientis, ib.14.1073; of a god, SIG56.26

ἀρωγή.definition: of persons, an aid, succour, of Apollo and Artemis, S.OC1094 ; of the Greek host, A.Ag.47, cf. 73 .—Poet. word, rare in Prose

ἀσάρωτος.definition: unswept, a room paved in mosaic to look as if strewn with crumbs, Plin.HN36.184

ἄσηπτος.definition: not liable to decay or corruption; undigested, Hp.Aff.24

ἄσθμα.definition: short-drawn breath, panting; Medic., asthma, Hp.Aph.3.22, etc

ἄσικχος.definition: not nice as to food, Plu.Lyc.16; not easily causing satiely or disgust, of food, Id.2.132b

ἄσιλλα.definition: yoke, like that of a milk-man, to carry baskets, pails, etc., Simon.163; Alciphr.1.1

ἀσιώπητος.definition: not to be left unspoken, Eun.Hist.p.261 D

ἀσκάλαφος.definition: an unknown bird, perh. a kind of owl, Arist.HA509a21

ἀσκαρίς.definition: worm in the intestines, Hp.Aph.3.26; larva of the ib.551b27

ἀσκελής.definition: dried up, withered; neut. as Adv., toughly, stubbornly, ib.1.68,4.543; Nic.Th.278:—also Il.19.68

ἀσκευής.definition: without the implements of his art; without furniture, Muson.Fr.14p.71H

ἄσκηνος.definition: without tents, not under canvas, Plu.Sert.12, App.BC5.117

ἀσκίτης.definition: kind of dropsy, ascites; patient suffering from the disease, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.8.9

ἄσκοπος.definition: inconsiderate, heedless; Pass., not to be seen, invisible, of the nether world, S.OC1682 , cf. E.Hyps.Fr.57.21

ᾆσμα.definition: song, esp. lyric ode, hymn, Pl.Prt.343csq., Alex.19, Luc.Salt.16; SIG648B7

ἄσπεδος.definition: dub. in Epich.42; perh. as Adj. shd. be read

ἀσπιδεῖον.definition: part of shield, IG2.720Bi 16; part of the prow of a ship, Id

ἀσπίς.definition: shield, Il.14.428, al.; Hdt.1.194; A.Th.489; Il.4.448, al.; opp. Thracian and Persian X.An.2.1.6, Mem.3.9.2; Anacr.28, Ar.V.19, cf. Hdt.5.95: to estimate a victory, X.HG1.2.3: metaph., A.Ag.1437; Nicostr. Com.29, cf. …

ἀθετέω.definition: set at naught a treaty, promise; c.dat., refuse one's assent, Plb.12.14.6

ἄθετος.definition: without position or place; not in its place, i.e. lying about, IG1.322i10,22

ἀθήρωμα.definition: tumour full of gruel-like matter , Gal.10.985, Heliod. ap. Orib.45.5 tit

ἀθλεύω.definition: Ep. and Ion. fut. A.Pr.95 , Q.S.4.113, Nonn.D.37.557:—contend for a prize, abs., Il.4.389, cf. 23.274,737, Hes.Th.435; once in Hdt.5.22: contr. once in Hom., struggling or suffering for him, Il.24.734; once in Pl., Lg…

ἀθλέω.definition: Ion. impf. Hdt.1.67, 7.212: aor; to be an athlete, contend in games, Simon.149, CIG2810b

ἄθλημα.definition: contest, struggle, Pl.Lg.833c, etc.: pl; implement of labour, Theoc.21.9

ἄθλησις.definition: contest, combat, esp. of athletes; generally, struggle, trial, Ep.Heb.10.32

ἄθολος.definition: not turbid, clear, Luc.Hist.Conscr.51: Sup., Olymp.in Mete.271.22

ἀθόρυβος.definition: without uproar, Pl.Lg.640c; unperturbed; not causing confusion, Ascl.Tact.12.10

ἀθρέω.definition: inspect, IG12.694; abs. or with a Prep., look earnestly, gaze, Il.10 11; observe, watch, A.Fr.226; look hither, E.Hipp.300; Id.Andr.1228; by observing, S.OC252; Ar.Av.1196

ἀθύρω.definition: Ep. word, only pres. and impf., rare in Prose :-play, sport, of children, Il.15.364, Hp.Ep.17; . . E.Ion53; . . Id.Fr.323; A.R.4.950; of dancing, Pl.Lg.796b; playing on an instrument, Anacreont.41.11: c. acc. cogn., s…

αἰγιάλειος.definition: frequenting the shore, Aët.2.141, Ath.Med. ap. Orib.inc.23.8

αἰγινόμος.definition: feeding goats: Subst; Pass., browsed by goats, ib.217

αἰδέομαι.definition: and poet. Hom., etc., Ep. imper; mostly c. acc., stand in awe of, fear, esp. in moral sense, Il.24.503, Od.9.269; Il.6.442, cf. Od.2.65, etc.; show a sense of regard one for another, Il.5.530; Od.21.28; respect the ho…

αἰέτιον χάριν ἐκτείσω.definition: prov. of those who repay benefits quickly, Apostol.1.78

αἴθαλος.definition: smoky flame, thick smoke, Hp.Mul.1.91 (as; grape grown in Egypt, Plin.HN 14.74

αἰθρία.definition: Ion. = first in Sol.13.22; esp. the clear cold air of night, Hdt.2.68, cf. Hp.Aët.8. in penult. exc. in dact. and anap., Sol. l.c., Ar. l.c.]

αἰθριάζω.definition: clear the sky, Arist.Pr.941a4:—also = in pf. part. Pass. Hp.Morb.3.17

αἰθριάω.definition: expose to the air, cool; intr., clear up, of the sky, Babr.45.9

αἴθω.definition: only pres. and impf., light up, kindle; rarely intr., burn, blaze, Pi.O.7.48; S.Aj.286

αἱματίζω.definition: stain with blood; of insects, draw blood, sting, Arist.HA532a13

αἱματόω.definition: make bloody, stain with blood; slay, aor. S.Fr.987

αἱμορροΐς.definition: mostly in pl., (sc; kind of shell-fish, perh. Aporrhais pes-pelicani, Arist.HA530a19

αἱμόρροος.definition: contr. flowing with; suffering from haemorrhoids, Hp.Epid.4.7

αἱμοσάτης.definition: a Samian earth used in burnishing gold, interp. in Dsc.5.154

αἰνετής.definition: one that praises, opp. dub. in Hp.de Arte8

αἰνέω.definition: impf. E.Hec.1154, Ion. Hdt.3.73: fut. Od.16.380, Thgn.1080, Pi.N.1.72; in Att. Poets always as in Pi.N.7.63, Semon.7.112: aor. Hom., opt. Simon.57.1; Dor. Pi.P.3.13; in Att. always Ion. Hdt.5.113: Isoc.12.207:- Med., …

αἰνοδρυφής.definition: sadly torn, in sign of mourning, Antim.[107]

αἴνυμαι.definition: poet. Verb, only in pres. and impf. without augm.:— take, Il.11.580, 13.550; Od.21.53; taking hold of, 22.500: c. gen. partit., 9.225: metaph., a longing seizes me for him, 14.144, cf. Hes.Sc.41; enjoy, feed on, Simon…

αἰξωνεύομαι.definition: Dep., to be slanderous, like the people of the Attic deme Aexone, Harp. s.v

αἰόλλω.definition: only pres., to shift rapidly to and fro; variegate, Nic.Th.155:—Pass., shift colour, Hes.Sc.399

αἱρετέος.definition: to be chosen, opp; one must choose, Pl.Grg.499e, Phld.Rh.1.287S., etc

αἱρετής.definition: searcher of archives; one who chooses, Vett.Val.55.17

αἱρέω.definition: impf. Il.24.579, Ion. Hdt.6.31, but; take away, Il.24.579

αἰσθάνομαι.definition: of mental perception, perceive, understand, Hp.Off.1; Lys.9.4, cf. Th.3.36, etc.:— hear, learn, v. infr. II: abs., you are right, E.Or.752; in parenthesis, Id.Hipp.1403

αἴσθημα.definition: object of sensation; sense or perception of a thing, E.IA1243

ἀΐσθω.definition: Ep. Verb, breathe out, he was giving up the ghost, Il.20.403, cf. 16.468

αἰσχύνη.definition: shame, dishonour; dishonouring of women, Isoc.4.114 , 12.259 ; for dishonour done to his race, Pl.Lg.919e

αἰσχύνω.definition: Ion. impf. Q.S.14.531; esp. dishonour a woman, E.El.44, cf. Plu.Marc.19, etc.; A.Ag.1626; Arist.Pol.1311b7; abs., Foed. Delph.Pell.2A 12

αἰτέω.definition: mostly c. acc. rei, ask for, demand, Il.5.358, Od.17.365, etc.; ask leave to depart, Od.10.17; to ask something for one, 20.74, Hdt.5.17: c. acc. pers. et rei, ask a person for a thing, Il.22.295, Od.2.387, Hdt.3.1, e…

αἰτία.definition: responsibility, mostly in bad sense, guilt; in forensic oratory, invective without proof , D.22.23, cf. 18.15

αἰτιάομαι.definition: used by Hom. only in Ep. forms, 3pl; in good sense, give one the credit of being, Pl.R.599e, cf. 379c, Cra.396d

αἰτίζω.definition: c. acc. pers., beg of, . . Od.17.346; abs., beg, ib.228, cf.4.651

αἰχμάζω.definition: Ep. fut. throw the spear; arm with the spear, S.Aj.97: metaph. of general's speech, Onos.1.13

αἰχμή.definition: point of a spear; generally, point, of arrows, A.Pers.239; Opp.H.1.216, C.2.451

αἰωρέω.definition: hang, Luc.JConf.4:—metaph., . . excited them to think that . . , App.BC2.81, cf. Plu.Brut.37.—Never in good Att

αἰώρημα.definition: that which is hung up or hovers; hanging cord, halter, E.Hel.353 ; hanging slings or chains, Id.Or.984

ἀκαθαρσία.definition: uncleanness, foulness, of a wound or; dirt, filth, BGU1117.27 , etc

ἀκαιρέω.definition: to be without an opportunity, opp; talk nonsense, Astramps.Orac.74.9

ἀκαιρία.definition: unfitness of times, opp; of bad seasons, unseasonableness, Pl.Lg.709a; Arist.Pr.941b25

ἀκαίριμος.definition: ill-timed: prov., quicquid in buccam venerit, Lyr.Adesp.86A

ἀκαίριος.definition: poet. for of untimely death, IG14.1363.11. Adv. unseasonably, BGU846.14

ἀκανθίας.definition: prickly thing, and so; kind of shark, prob. Squalus acanthias L., Arist.HA565a29, 621b17

ἀκανθίς.definition: a bird, goldfinch, Fringilla; = Call. ap. Plin.HN25.168: = Ps.-Dsc.3.13: = ib.16

ἀκανθολάβος.definition: instrument for extracting thorns, ibid.:—also Gloss

ἀκαχίζω.definition: only pres., trouble, grieve, Od.16.432:—Med., . . be not troubled, Il.6.486: c. part., Od.11.486

ἀκέομαι.definition: Ion. imper. Hdt.3.40; trans., heal, cure, c. acc. of thing healed, Il.16.523; 16.29; Hdt.4.90; of part healed, Hp.Mochl.25; S.Tr.1035; E.Hec.1067; . . Il.5.448, cf. 402: c. gen. morbi, . . Epigr.Gr.803 , cf. Paus.8.18.8

ἀκερδής.definition: bringing no gain, unprofitable; not greedy of gain, Id.Arist.1. Adv. Id.2.483e

ἀκεστήρ.definition: healer: Adj., rein that tames the steed, S.OC714

ἀκέστρια.definition: sempstress, Antip. Tars.Stoic.3.254, Luc.Rh.Pr.24; title of play by Antiphanes: in pl., title of mime by Sophron

ἀκέω.definition: to be silent, only opt. pres. A.R.1.765

ἀκηδιάω.definition: to be careless, Zos.Alch.p.133B; to be exhausted, weary, LXXPs.60.2, etc

ἀκιδόω.definition: furnish with barb or point, in Pass., IG2.807

ἄκληρος.definition: without lot or portion, poor, needy; unallotted, without owner, h.Ven.123, E.Tr.32

ἀκλήρωτος.definition: without lot or portion in a thing, c; without casting lots, D.C.Fr.62

ἄκλοπος.definition: not guilty of peculation; not furtively concealed, Opp.H.3.532

ἄκνηστις.definition: spine or backbone of animals; stinging-nettle, = Nic.Th.52

ἀκολουθέω.definition: follow one, go after or with him, freq. of; of stars, follow in the diurnal rotation, Autol.2.2

ἀκοντίζω.definition: Att. fut. hurl a javelin; after Hom., hit or strike with javelin, or simply aim at, Hdt.1.43, etc.:—Pass., to be hit or wounded, E.Ba.1098, Antipho3.1.1, X.HG4.5.13

ἄκοπος.definition: unwearied, Pl.Lg.789d. Adv; free from trouble, Amips.28

ἄκοπρος.definition: with little excrement in the bowels; = foreg., Thphr.HP8.6.4

ἀκορία.definition: not eating to satiety, moderation in; insatiable desire of drink, Aret.CD2.2

ἄκοσμος.definition: disorderly, A.Pers.470; a world that is no world, AP7.561 , but in 9.323 of an inappropriate ornament

ἀκοστάω.definition: or only aor. part., horse well-fed at rack and manger, Il.6.506, 15.263; cf

ἀκουάζομαι.definition: hear, listen to, c. gen., Od.9.7, cf. 13.9; ye are bidden to the feast, like Il.4.343: Medic., of auscultation, Hp.Morb.2.61:—Act., h.Merc.423

ἄκουσμα.definition: thing heard, such as music; rumour, report, S.OC518 , Jul.Or.3.110d

ἀκούω.definition: Ep. impf. Il.12.442: fut; in Prose the pers. from whom thing is heard freq. takes Prep., first in Il.6.524, cf. Hdt.3.62, S.OT7,95, Th.1.125

ἀκράχολος.definition: quick to anger irascible; generally, in passionate distress, Theoc.24.61. ; is freq. v.l. in codd. of early authors, as Pl. l. c.)

ἀκρίβωμα.definition: exact knowledge; consummate display of execution, in music, Phld. Mus.p.90 K

ἀκρόασις.definition: hearing, hearkening or listening; thing listened to, recitation, lecture, Hp.Praec.,12, Plb.32.2.5, IG2.466, title of work by Arist

ἀκροατής.definition: hearer, of persons who come to hear; reader, Plu.Thes.1, Lys.12

ἀκροβαρέω.definition: become top-heavy, lose balance by being overloaded at the extremity, Apollod.Poliorc.164.3, 166.10

ἀκροβατέω.definition: walk on tiptoe, strut, of ostriches; climb aloft, Polyaen.4.3.23

ἀκροκελαινιάω.definition: only used in Ep. part. growing black on surface, of swollen stream, Il.21.249; cf. Nonn.D.18.156

ἀκροπόλος.definition: high-ranging, lofly; Subst., arctic and antarctic circles, Olymp.in Mete.183.30

ἀκροπόρος.definition: boring through, piercing with the; proparox., Pass., with opening at end, Nonn.D.2.2

ἀκτάζω.definition: banquet on the shore, enjoy oneself

ἀκταίνω.definition: = foreg., keep my stature erect, A.Eu.36: metaph., Trag.Adesp.147; cf

ἀκύμων.definition: gen. without fruit, barren, of women, E.Andr.158; of the earth, Moschio Trag.8

ἀλαζών.definition: prop. wanderer about; charlatan, quack, esp. of Sophists, Cratin.380, Ar.Nu.102, Pl.Chrm.173c, al

ἀλαλάω.definition: make dumb, in Pass., Aq.Ps.38.3; but Pass., ib.30.19

ἀλάλημαι.definition: pf. of only in pres. sense , wander, roam about, like a beggar, Hom. mostly in Od.,2.370, 15.10, etc.; of seamen, 3.72, cf. 313; of a departed spirit, Il.23.74; of things, Hes.Op.100 :—once Trag., in plpf., E.Andr.306

ἀλαλύκτημαι.definition: to be in anguish, sore distressed, pf. formed by redupl. from Il.10.94

ἀλάομαι.definition: Ep. 3pl. imper. (v; c. gen., wander away from, miss a thing, Pi.O.1.58; E.Tr.640

ἀλαόω.definition: blind, blind him of his eye, Od.1.69, 9.516: c. acc., AP7.601

ἀλαπάζω.definition: Ep. impf. Il.11.503: fut. 2.367, A.Ag.130 : Ep. aor. Il.11.750, Thgn.951 :—Pass., Il.24.245 :—empty, drain, exhaust, Od.17.424; sack, plunder, Il.2.367; of men, overpower, destroy, 5.166, 31.503, al.: metaph., Panyas.14

ἀλαστέω.definition: to be full of wrath or to be distraught, Il.15.21; . . 12.163, cf. Call.Del.239, Musae.202, etc., cf. Gal.Lex. s.v

ἀλγέω.definition: fut. Od.12.27, feel bodily pain; suffer hardship, Od.l.c

ἀλγίων.definition: irreg. Comp. and Sup. of formed fr. Subst. : —more or most painful, grievous, or distressing: — of Comp., Hom. has only neut. in signf. so much the worse, . . Il.18.278, cf. 306, Od.4.292: Sup. only in Il.23.655 .— Bo…

ἄλγυνσις.definition: causing of pain, Phlp.in de An.17.33; opp. Olymp.in Grg.p.531 J

ἀλδαίνω.definition: only pres. and impf., exc. Ep.aor. 3sg. , Orph.L.370 :—causal of make to grow, nourish, strengthen, she filled out his limbs, Od.18.70, 24.368, cf. A.Th.12; Id.Pr.539; increase, multiply, . . Id.Th.557 :— Pass., Aglaï…

ἀλεγίζω.definition: Ep. Verb, used only in pres. and impf.: :— trouble oneself about a thing, care for, mind, heed, in Hom. always with neg., c. gen., Il.1.160, al.; 11.80, cf. Hes.Th.171 : abs., Il.15.106; in late Ep. c. acc., Q.S.2.428…

ἀλεγύνω.definition: Ep. Verb, Hom. only pres. and impf.: aor. A.R.1.394, Med. Emp.137.4 : :—heed, care for, Hom. always c. acc. or find your meals elsewhere, 1.374; of invited guests, 13.23; but . . prepare a meal for guests, 11.186; h.M…

ἀλέγω.definition: Ep. and Lyr., once in A. , only pres; abs., have no care, Il.11.389, Od.17.390; Od.19.154: without neg., walk with good heed, Il.9.504

ἀλεείνω.definition: Ep., only pres. and impf. (exc. aor; intr., shrink, A.R.3.650

ἀλείπτρια.definition: fem. of Lys.Fr.88S.; title of plays by Amphis, Antiph., etc

ἀλείφω.definition: Hdt.3.8, etc.: fut. LXXEx.40.15; supply oil for gymnasts, CIG 1957g ; Inscr.Magn.163, OGI533.47 ; youths undergoing gymnastic training, ib.339.72 , etc.; ib.764.5 , al.; to attend a gymnastic school, Arr.Epict.1.2.26

ἀλέκω.definition: = ward off, prob. for AP6.245 :—for fut. etc., v. sub

ἀλέξησις.definition: keeping off, defence; helping, assistance, Hp.Ep.16

ἀλέξω.definition: Ep. inf. Hom., v. infr.: fut. Il.9.251: aor. opt. Od.3.346:-Med., fut. Hdt.8.81,108.-Besides these tenses , we find others formed from aor. :- Med., fut. S.OT171,539, X.An.7.7.3: aor. Il., Hp.Salubr.1, Hdt.7.207, X.An…

ἀλέομαι.definition: contr. Thgn.575, pres.part. Hes.Op.535 , Semon.7.61: impf. Il.18.586:- chiefly used by Hom. in aor. v. infr.; inf. Hes.Op.734,505; subj. Od.14.400; part. 9.277, Thgn.400. :-avoid, shun, c. acc. rei, Il.6.226, cf. 13.1…

ἀλετρεύω.definition: fut. Lyc.159, strengthd. from grind, Od.7.104, Hes.Fr.264, A.R.4.1095, Babr.129

ἀλετρίς.definition: female slave who grinds corn; at Athens, one of the noble maidens who prepared meal for offering-cakes, Ar.Lys.643, Eust.1885.9

ἀλετών.definition: = upper millstone, Alex.13; also alone, Dieuchid.7

ἀλεύω.definition: used rarely by Trag. in lyr. passages as Act. of (v. remove, keep far away, imper. A.Fr.567: fut. S.Fr.993: aor. imper., A.Supp.528, cf. Th.141; . . ib.87

ἀλέω.definition: impf. Pherecr.10.1: aor. Id.183,Hp.Fist.7, Steril.230, etc.; Ep. Od.20.109: pf. AP11.251 :—Pass., pf. Hp. ap. Gal.19.76, Hdt.7.23; Th.4.26, Amph.9: aor. Dsc.1.120:—grind, bruise, Hom. only in compd. q. v.; Pherecr.l.c…

ἀλητεύω.definition: Dor. fut. E.Heracl.515:—wander, roam, mostly of beggars, Od.17.501, al., AP9.12 ; of hunters, Od.12.330; of exiles, E.l.c., Hipp.1048, Phalar.Ep.95; Ph.1.463

ἁλιεύω.definition: fish, Ev.Jo.21.3; to be a fisher; only Med. occurs in Att., Pl.Com.44; title of play by Antiph.:—also later, Posidon.68

ἁλιηγής.definition: broken on by the sea, Opp.H.3.460

ἀλίνδησις.definition: rolling in dust, exercise in which wrestlers rolled on the ground, Hp.Vict.2.64, 3.68, Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.2.11

ἁλιόω.definition: poet. Verb, only fut. aor. Ep; destroy, . . Id.OC704

ἁλιπόρος.definition: through which the sea flows, Luc.Trag.24

ἁλίσκομαι.definition: defect. Pass., Act. supplied by; to be caught, seized, of persons and things, to be seized by death, die, Il.21.281, Od.5.312; without Il.12.172, Od.18.265, etc.; Pi.P.3.57; letters were seized and taken to Athens, X.…

ἀλιταίνω.definition: Ep. Verb, used by A. in lyr., chiefly; c.acc. rei, transgress, Il.24.570; A.R.4.388, Opp.H.5.563

ἁλίτροχος.definition: rushing through the sea, Ibyc.50, in metapl. acc. sing

ἀλκτήρ.definition: one who wards off, protector from a thing, c. gen., Il.18.100, Od.14.531; Pi.P.3.7

ἄλλαγμα.definition: that which is given or taken in; reward, price of a thing, AP12.132 , LXXDe.23.18

ἀλλοδοξία.definition: mistaking of one thing for another; revolutionary spirit, D.C.79.5

ἀλλόδοξος.definition: holding a different opinion, belonging to a different school, Phld.Herc.19.2

ἅλλομαι.definition: h.Cer.175, etc.: impf. X.Cyr.1.4.11; c. acc., leap over, Ael.NA6.6; Opp.C.1.83

ἀλλοπαθής.definition: properly, subject to external; Adv. of Verbs, transitively, Eust.920.27

ἀλλοφρονέω.definition: Ep. and Ion., think of other; to be of another mind, have other views, v.l. in Hdt.7.205

ἀλλοφυής.definition: changed in shape, Nonn.D.4.419, al; of strange, abnormal shape, ib.2.148, al

ἅλμη.definition: after Hom., brine, i.e. the sea, Arion1.3, Pi.P.4.39, A.Pers.397, Tim.Pers.96, etc

ἀλοάω.definition: Ep. Theoc.10.48: Ep. impf; thresh, smite, Il.0.568, cf. Epigr. l.c.; Plu.TG2; cudgel, thrash, Glotta l. c., S.Fr.20 , Ar.Ra.149, Herod.2.34; Babr.98.15

ἀλογέω.definition: pay no regard to thing; to be unreasonable, Phld.Ir.p.34 W

ἀλοκίζω.definition: prop. trace furrows: hence, write, draw, with play on words, Ar.V.850:—Pass., pf. part. scratched, torn, Lyc.119,381

ἀλυπέω.definition: to be free from pain, imper. IG14.1030, etc.; prob. l. in Phld.Rh.1.373S

ἀλυπία.definition: freedom from pain or grief, Antipho Soph; digestibility, Thphr.HP2.4.2

ἀλυσκάζω.definition: strengthd. for ; irreg. opt. Nonn.D.42.135, al.:—shun, avoid, c. acc., Od.17.581: abs., skulk, Il.5.253, 6.443, Orph.A.437; dub. in Hes.Fr.96.94.—Ep. word, used by Cratin.137

ἀλυσμός.definition: anguish, disquiet: esp. tossing about, of sick persons, Hp.Prog.3, al

ἀλύσσω.definition: v. infr., to be uneasy, restless, pres. only Il.22.70 fut., will be restless . . , Hp.Mul.1.2: plpf. Pass., was disquieted, Q.S.14.24

ἀλύω.definition: Att. acc. to Suid., cf. Eust.1636.28, Aeol; from grief, to be distraught, beside oneself, Il.5.352; 24.12; in mad passion, Od.9.398; S.El.135; E.Or.277, etc

ἀλωπεκίς.definition: mongrel between fox and dog, =; fox-skin cap, X.An.7.4.4

ἁλώσιμος.definition: easy to take or conquer, of; of the mind, easy to apprehend, S.Ph.863

ἅλωσις.definition: Ion. capture, Pi.O.10.42; taking, catching of birds and fish, Arist.HA593a20, 600a3 ; taken without power to escape, Plu.Num.15

ἀμαθής.definition: ignorant, stupid, Hdt.1.33; of moral defects, unfeeling, inhuman, E.HF347

ἀμαθύνω.definition: Ep., only pres., impf., and (in; scatter like sand, h.Merc.140

ἀμαλδύνω.definition: Ep. and Ion. word; metaph., conceal, disguise, h.Cer.94, cf. A.R.1.834; efface, Id.4.112

ἄμαλλα.definition: bundle of ears of corn; poet. for corn, Q.S.11.156, 171, etc

ἁμαξεύω.definition: traverse with a wagon:—Pass., to be traversed; metaph., drag on a weary life, AP9.574

ἁμαρτάνω.definition: fut. Od.9.512, Th.4.55, etc.; later Ev.Matt.18.21, D.C.59.20, Gal.7.653, Hp.Praec.9, Id.Acut. 13: aor. 2 Thgn., Pi., Att.; Ep. but only ind.; Aeol. 3sg. Sapph.Supp.1.5, inf. IG12.1.15 ; opt. Cratin.55 : aor. 1 Emp.115…

ἀμαρύσσω.definition: Ep., only pres. and impf., sparkle; Act., shoot forth, dart, h.Merc.415, Q.S.8.29

ἀμαυρόω.definition: Sol. and X., v.infr.: fut. Simon.4.5; render invisible, PMag. Berol.1.102

ἀμαύρωμα.definition: obscuration, of sun, Plu.Caes.69; dimness of sight, Mnesith. ap. Orib.4.4.2

ἀμάω.definition: Od.9.135, etc.; Ep. pres. part; metaph., Plu.2.210b

ἀμβλυντήρ.definition: causing dimness of sight, in pl., Poet.de herb.65

ἀμβλωπής.definition: abortive, of the flowers of the vine, Thphr.CP3.15.2

ἀμβροσία.definition: Ion. immortality, rarein; in religious rites, mixture of water, oil, and various fruits, Anticl.13

ἀμείβω.definition: Il., Trag.: Ep. impf. Il.14.381; give in exchange, ib.6.235: c.acc., E.Alc.46: or more freq

ἀμέλγω.definition: fut. Theoc.23.25, milk, with acc. of; suck up moisture, of the sun, Nonn.D.2.500

ἀμελέω.definition: aor. Ep. Il., v. infr.: pf; abs., to be careless, negligent, Hes.Op.400, freq. in Att., Isoc.9.78, etc.; A.Eu.86; S.El.237

ἀμέλητος.definition: not to be cared for, unworthy of care, Thgn.422. Adv. heedlessly, Luc.Tim.12

ἀμεμφία.definition: freedom from blame, mediator has no freedom from blame on the part of his friends, A.Th.909; for avoidance of censure, S.Fr.283

ἀμενηνόω.definition: weaken, deaden the force of, Il.13.562

ἀμέρδω.definition: Orph.L.169: aor. poet; c. acc. pers. only, bereave of natural rights, Il.16.53; blinded the eyes, ib.13.340, cf. Hes.Th.698; . . robs of their lustre, tarnishes, Od.19.18

ἀμερής.definition: without parts, indivisible, Pl.Tht.205e; in Logic, summa genera, Arist.APo.100b2

ἀμετρία.definition: excess, disproportion, opp; want of moderation, Arist.VV1251b15

ἀμηχανία.definition: Ion. want of means or; of things, hardship, trouble, Hes.Op.496

ἀμισθία.definition: non-receipt of pay, App.Hann.17; of free teaching, Olymp.in Alc.p.140C

ἀμοιβάς.definition: pecul. fem. of foreg., . . which lay beside him as change of raiment, Od.14.521; in succession, Nonn.D.28.135

ἀμοιβή.definition: requital, recompense, Hom. only in; repayment, compensation, Od.12.382

ἀμοιβός.definition: one who exchanges, soldiers that; Adj. in requital or exchange for, S.Ant.1067; AP7.341

ἀμορβάς.definition: fem. of in A.R.3.881 rural or attendant Nymphs

ἀμορβεύω.definition: follow, attend, c. dat., Nic.Fr.90:—Med., let follow, make follow, Antim.23

ἀμουσία.definition: want of education, taste or refinement; want of harmony, E.HF676

ἄμουσος.definition: without song, of fishes, Emp.74; but usu; of persons, unmusical, Id.Sph.253b, al

ἄμοχθος.definition: free from toil and trouble, of persons; not tired, X.Mem.2.1.33

ἀμπέχω.definition: surround, cover, enclose, Od.6.225; S.OC314, cf. A.l.c.: metaph., invest one with . . , Pl.Prt.320e: abs., surrounding darkness, E.Hipp.192; of the wooden horse, Id.Tr.12; Aret.SA2.2

ἀμυντήρ.definition: lit. defender: brow- tines of stag's antlers, Arist.HA611b5

ἀμύντωρ.definition: poet. word, defender, helper; repeller, Simon.86

ἀμύνω.definition: Ep. impf. Il.15.731: fut; c.acc. of the person or thing to be kept off, c. dat. pers. for or from whom danger averted, ward off ruin from the Danai, Il.1.456, cf. 341, Od.8.525:—dat. freq. omitted, Il.5.603; Pl.Lg.692…

ἀμύσσω.definition: Att. Phld.Lib.p.57 O.: Ep. impf; metaph., thou wilt tear thy heart with rage, Il.1.243, cf. Call.Aet.3.1.10; B.16.19, cf. 17.11, A.Pers.161; ib.116; Aeschin.l.c., cf. Phld. l.c., Jul.Or.2.96a

ἀμυχή.definition: scratch, skin-wound, Hp.Epid.7.32; Medic., scarification, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.18.3, Gal.10.964

ἀμφαγαπάζω.definition: used by Hom. only in impf. pres. part. Med. by later Ep. only in pres., impf., cf. IG12.289.14 :—embrace with love, greet warmly, Od.14.381, Canthar.2 D. , A.R.3.258, etc.; so Med., Il.16.192, h.Cer.290

ἀμφαγείρομαι.definition: Med., gather round, Hom. only in aor. 2, Il.18.37, cf. A.R.4.1527: in later Ep. pres. Theoc.17.94, Opp.H.3.231, 4.114

ἀμφαξονέω.definition: go unsteadily, totter: metaph. from wheels loose on axles, Paus.Gr.Fr.50

ἀμφαραβέω.definition: Ep., rattle or ring around, in Ep. impf. Hes.Sc.64

ἀμφαφάω.definition: touch or feel all round; of persons, easier to deal with, Il.22.373.—Ep. Verb used by Aret. in forms SD2.4, CA1.1; ib.2.4; cf. Hsch

ἀμφέλκω.definition: draw around: Med., draw a thing round one, i.e. be surrounded by it, D.P.268

ἀμφέρχομαι.definition: surround, Hom. only aor. 2, c. acc; intr., pass, elapse, of time, GDI4999

ἀμφιάζω.definition: Plu.CG2 : fut. Alciphr.3.42: aor. AP7.368 , OGI200.24 , Polyaen.1.27.2 , Philostr.Her.Prooem.2: pf. Clearch.25:—Med., fut. Luc.Herm.86 codd.: aor. Apollod.2.1.2, etc.: pf. in med. sense D.S.16.11 :— is a common v.l.: …

ἀμφιβαίνω.definition: fut. etc.:—go about or around; bestride, he bestrode a beam, Od.5.371, Call.Del.113; of a cock, Babr.5.8: esp

ἀμφιβάλλω.definition: fut. etc.:—Med., Ep. fut; of clothes, etc., put them on a person, c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, . . Od.10.365, cf. 451; . . 13.434: c. dat. pers., . . v.l. in 14.342; . . Il.18.204; . . E.HF465; Pi.P.5.32:—Med., put rou…

ἀμφιδαίω.definition: kindle around: —only intr. in pf. and plpf., burn, blaze around, Il.6.329; 12.35; of dust, Hes.Sc.62

ἀμφιδάκνω.definition: bite all round: hence, grip close, APl.4.118

ἀμφιδινέομαι.definition: Pass., to be put round in a circle, Hom. in pf. only, round whose edge a stream of tin is rolled, Il.23.562; scabbard is fitted close round it, Od.8.405; of persons, to be dizzy, Aret.SD2.3

ἀμφίδοξος.definition: of persons, with doubtful mind; of a witness, of doubtful credibility, Arist.Rh.Al.1431b23

ἀμφιέννυμι.definition: rarely c. dat. rei. clothe one in or with, Pl.Prt.321a: metaph., cloak . . , D.H.6.16

ἀμφιέπω.definition: beset, press hard, Il.11.483; so perh. in Od.3.118; to be busy about, look after, Il.24.804, cf. 5.667; dressed the meat, 11.776; Od.8.61, Il.24.622:—do honour or reverence to, Pi.O.6.95; tend or heal sick, P.3.51; sw…

ἀμφιζάνω.definition: sit on, c. dat., ashes settled upon the tunic, Il.18.25

ἀμφιθέω.definition: generally pres., run round about, Od.10.413: c. dat., right mind surrounds him, Mosch.2.107: impf. Q.S.5.371

ἀμφικαλύπτω.definition: fut. A.R.2.583: aor. v. infr; c.acc., enwrap, enfold, of garments, Il.2.262; of a coffin, 23.91; received within it, Od.8.511, cf. 4.618; love enfolded my senses, Il.3.442; 5.68, cf. 12.116; 16.350; 11.356; Od.5.493; …

ἀμφικεάζω.definition: cleave asunder, in Ep. aor. part. Od.14.12

ἀμφιμάχομαι.definition: Ep. Verb, only pres and impf., fight; c. acc., assail, besiege, Il.6.461; 9.412; 16.73

ἀμφιμυκάομαι.definition: properly of cattle, low all around: metaph., floor echoed to song [of Circe], Od.10.227

ἀμφιμωλέω.definition: sue at law concerning, Leg.Gort.1.2, cf.9.19:—hence subject of legal process, 10.27

ἀμφινέμομαι.definition: Med., dwell round, c. acc. loci, Il.2.521; of gods, 18.186; Od.19.132; of constellations, Arat.282: abs., D.P.127, al.: metaph., encompasses thee, Pi.P.5.14

ἀμφινεύω.definition: nod this way and that, AP9.709

ἀμφιπέλομαι.definition: hover, float around, of music, Od.1.352; encompass, Sammelb.5829.16

ἀμφιπένομαι.definition: Ep. only pres. and impf., =; dogs made not a meal of him, Il.23.184, cf. 21.203; . . hem in, A.R.2.27

ἀμφιπεριστέφομαι.definition: Pass., to be put round as a crown, grace crowns not his words, Od.8.175

ἀμφιπεριστρωφάω.definition: Frequent. of keep turning about all ways, Il.8.348:—Pass., Q.S.13.11

ἀμφιπιάζω.definition: Dor. for squeeze all round, hug closely, Theoc.Ep.6.4

ἀμφιπίπτω.definition: poet. fall upon and embrace, embrace eagerly, c. acc., Od.8.523, cf. Parth.15.2; E.Supp.278: c. dat., embracing so as to kiss, S.Tr.938; fall over, Parth.8.4: metaph., take to one's heart, Pi.O.10.98

ἀμφιπλήξ.definition: striking with both sides, Id.Tr.930: metaph., of a father's and mother's curse, OT417

ἀμφιπολεύω.definition: Ep. Verb mostly in pres; abs., . . Od.20.78, cf. Hes.Op.803; hold the yearly office of IG12.906

ἀμφιπονέομαι.definition: attend to, provide for; Pass., neighbouring parts affected, Hp.Mul.2.135

ἀμφιποτάομαι.definition: fly round and round, of a bird, Il.2.315, cf. Sapph.Supp.14.4, Q.S.5.12

ἀμφίστημι.definition: place round: in this sense only poet. in; Med., investigate, Tab.Heracl.1.125; cf

ἀμφιστρατάομαι.definition: Dep., beleaguer, besiege, Ep. impf. Il.11.713

ἀμφιτεύχω.definition: make or work round about, plpf. Pass., of sea round shield of Achilles, Q.S.5.14

ἀμφιτίθημι.definition: rarely c. dat. rei, cover with a thing, E.Hec.432

ἀμφιτρής.definition: = sq.; rock pierced through, cave with double entrance, E.Cyc.707: also neut., S.Ph.19

ἀμφιφοβέομαι.definition: Pass., fear, tremble, or quake all round, Il.16.290 , cf. Q.S.2.546, 11.117

ἀμφιχάσκω.definition: impf., v. infr.: aor. round, gape for, c. acc., Il.23.79; of an infant, A.Ch.545; of the Argive army round Thebes, S.Ant.118; . . of a fish, AP7.702 : rarely c. dat., Opp.H.3.178

ἀμφιχέω.definition: pour around, pour or spread over; mostly Pass., to be poured or shed around, Il.23.764: c. acc., ib.2.41; Od.4.716; Mimn.5; we have ashes poured over our head, E.Supp.826

ἄμφοισμα.definition: revolving figure, Papp.682.8, 11:—hence described by revolution, 682.8,15

ἀναβαίνω.definition: impf. fut. (for aor. 1; mount a ship, go on board, in Hom. mostly abs.; embark for Troy, Od.1.210; 14.252; Th.4.44, etc.: metaph., I will mount a prow, Pi.P.2.62

ἀναβάλλω.definition: put on horseback, mount him, Id.An.4.4.4, Eq.6.12; of the horse, unseat his rider, ib.8.7

ἀναβράζω.definition: intr., boil or foam up, v.l. for Procop.Goth.3.35: also trans., Aët.1.226

ἀναγεννάω.definition: beget anew, regenerate, 1 Ep.Pet.1.3, cf; metaph., arouse afresh, Phld.Ir.p.18W

ἀναγιγνώσκω.definition: Ep. only in aor. 2; know well, know certainly, Od.1.216, cf. 21.205, Il.13.734

ἀναγλυφή.definition: work in low relief, Aristeas58; scooped out cavity, Herophil. ap.Gal.2.731

ἀναγνάμπτω.definition: bend back, the spear-point; undo, loose, Od.14.348

ἀνάγω.definition: fut. etc.: aor. 2; lead up from a lower place to a higher, Thgn.1347, E.Ba.289; X.An.3.4.28; of the Trojan horse, E.Tr.525; Pl.Euthphr.6c

ἀναγωγή.definition: leading up, esp. taking a ship into the; bringing upstream, of a ship, OGI56.51

ἀναδέρκομαι.definition: Dep., look up, aor. 2 Act. of one who recovers from fainting, Il.14.436, cf. A.R.3.1010

ἀναδέχομαι.definition: fut. aor. Ep. aor; receive, entertain as a guest, Act.Ap.28.7

ἀναδικάζω.definition: decide again, hear on appeal; Med., renew an action after a previous judgement had been cancelled, Is.Fr.145

ἀναδρέπω.definition: break off, pluck, Nonn.D.9.120:—Med., cull, Them.Or.27.332d

ἀναδρομή.definition: running up: hence, sprouting, impulse; climbing up, of a tree, Agatharch.51

ἀνάδρομος.definition: running up, of a fish entering a river from the sea, Alex.Trall.1.15

ἀναδύνω.definition: come to the top of the water, Batr.90, Arist.Fr.335; of rivers which have disappeared into the earth, emerge, Id.Mete.356a25

ἀναείρω.definition: lift up, of a wrestler, Il.23.724; took them, carried them off, ib.614,778; 7.130:—Med., lift up in one's arms, carry off, A.R.4.94:—Pass., arise, A.R.1.1078; of a ship, leave the stocks, Orph.A.268

ἀναέξω.definition: enlarge, increase, Q.S.1.460; make grow, Coluth.247:—Pass., grow, Nonn.D.38.184, al.; grow into, be changed into, ib.44.243

ἀναζάω.definition: inf. return to life, be alive again, Ev.Luc.15.24 and 32, Sotionp.183 W.: in Ep. form Nic.Fr.70.5

ἀναζέω.definition: fut. boil up, bubble up; boil, swarm with worms, metaph., of Alexander's empire, Plu.2.337a; Id.Art.16

ἀναζωγρέω.definition: recall to life, of those in imminent danger; restore to life, Nonn.D.19.102

ἀναζώννυμι.definition: or fut. gird up again; Med., c. acc., embark on, Eust.Epiph.p.361 D

ἀναθέω.definition: run up, Ael.NA5.54, etc.: c. acc; of plants, shoot up, ib.2.36; . . Gal.18.178

ἀναθλίβω.definition: simply, press, AP12.208; of reducing a rupture, Archig. ap. Aët.9.28

ἀναθρῴσκω.definition: poet. and Ion. aor. 2 X.Lac.2.3: aor. 1 subj. Opp.H.3.293:—spring up, Il.13.140; of blood, Emp.100.8; of men, Hdt.7.18, cf. AP9.774 ; Hdt.3.64

ἀναθυρόω.definition: dress vertical joints of masonry so that only their edges are in contact, IG7.3073.121,142

ἀναθύω.definition: dart up, burst forth, Call.Cer.30; sacrifice again, in Pass., D.C.37.46

ἀναίθω.definition: light up, set on fire, E.Cyc.331

ἀναίνομαι.definition: impf. Ep. late also; c. acc., refuse or reject with contempt, spurn, Il.9.679; ib.510; on no one of the rest do I turn my back, Od.8.212; and without a notion of contempt, refused, declined to do it, ib.3.265; 'twould…

ἀναίρετος.definition: incapable of choosing; Pass., opp. Simp.in Epict.p.14 D., al

ἀναιρέω.definition: take up and carry off, bear away, esp. prizes, Il.23.736, cf.551; Hdt.5.102; 6.36, cf. B.I.1

ἀναΐσσω.definition: Att. contr. used also by; c. acc., . . having leapt upon it, Il.24.440

ἀναισχυντέω.definition: to be to be shameless; trans., treat shamelessly, and Pass., to be so treated, ib.1412a6

ἀνακαίω.definition: Att. aor. E.Cyc.383:—kindle; Pass., fire up with anger, Hdt.5.19; D.H.9.27

ἀνακαλέω.definition: poet. call up or back, esp. of; call again and again; and so

ἀνακείρω.definition: shear or cut off, rip up, Str.16.4.15, [Gal.]14.790, Aët.13.4

ἀνακηκίω.definition: spout up, gush forth; rare in Prose, bubble up, throb violently, Pl.Phdr.251b

ἀνακλίνω.definition: poet. lean one thing; Pass., of ground, lie sloping upwards, Gp.2.3.1

ἀνάκλισις.definition: lying or leaning back, position in; bending back, in tetanus, Aret.SA1.6

ἀνακμάζω.definition: break out afresh with renewed vigour, of J.BJ5.1.1

ἀνακνάπτω.definition: make old clothes fresh by fulling: metaph., vamp them up as new, Lysipp.4

ἀνακοντίζω.definition: intr., dart or shoot up; causal, Callistr.Stat.14

ἀνακόπτω.definition: drive back, push back; beat back an assailant, Th.4.12, cf. Plu.Caes.38

ἀνακράζω.definition: fut. or fut. pf; rarely of animals, Men.534.11

ἀνακρούω.definition: poet. push back a gate-pin; thrust her off from shore, A.R.4.1650; throw up, Philostr.Her.2.5

ἀνακυμβαλιάζω.definition: only in Il.16.379 the chariots fall rattling over

ἀνακωκύω.definition: wail aloud, A.Pers.468, cf. S.Ant.1227; . . utters a loud shrill wailing cry, ib.423

ἀναλέγω.definition: Ep. impf. : fut; in Med., reckon up, Plu.Lyc.1:— Pass. , being recounted, X.An.2.1.17

ἀναλειόω.definition: grind, rub down again, Pelag.Alch.p.255 B

ἀναλέκτης.definition: Lat. -lecta, slave who picked up broken meats, Mart.7.20

ἀναλθής.definition: not to be healed, Hp.Art.63; not healing, powerless to heal, BionFr.13.4

ἀναλογία.definition: mathematical proportion; proportion generally, Arist.Pol.1296b25, cf. Epicur.Nat.11.7,10

ἀναλύζω.definition: lit. hiccough: hence, sob aloud, Luc.Somn.4

ἀναλύτης.definition: deliverer, esp. from a magic spell, Magn.4

ἀναλύω.definition: cause to wander, unsettle, Philostr.VA5.35; unloose, set free, ib.12.200 , cf. Ant.Lib.22.4; Pi.N.10.90; Ael.VH5.18

ἀνάλωμα.definition: freq. in Pap. and; exhalation, Plu.2.384a codd

ἀνάλωτος.definition: metaph., unassailable, convincing, Pl.Tht.179c; of persons, incorruptible, X.Ages.8.8: c. gen., Men.Rh.p.416S

ἀναλωφάω.definition: to be relieved again, have a respite from suffering, Aret.CA2.11

ἀναμάσσω.definition: Med., knead one's bread, Ar.Nu.676 codd., cf. AB391; receive an impression, Ti.Locr.94a; of the eyes, Arr.Epict.2.23.3; Plot.4.3.26; Alex.Aphr.de An.137.1

ἀναμέλπω.definition: raise a strain, c. acc. cogn; trans., praise in song, Anacreont.36.2

ἀναμένω.definition: poet. Aeol. Alc.41:—wait for; put off, delay, X.Cyr.1.6.10: c. inf., D.19.224

ἀναμετρέω.definition: measure back again, re-measure the road; enumerate, Hp.Ep.27:—in Med., recapitulate, E.Or.14

ἀναμιμνήσκω.definition: fut. poet. Aeol. aor; c. acc. pers. et inf., remind one to do, Pi.P.4.54

ἀναμίμνω.definition: poet. for c. acc., Il.11.171: abs., 16.363

ἀναμορμύρω.definition: roar loudly, boil up, of Charybdis, Od.12.238, cf. Jul.Or.2.60d

ἀνανέμω.definition: poet. distribute: hence, count up, in; read, con over, Epich.224, Theoc.18.48

ἀνανεύω.definition: fut. Pl.R.350e, Luc.Sat.1; c. acc. rei, deny, refuse, Il.16.250: c. fut. inf., 16.252:—Pass., rejected, Ph.1.146

ἀνανήφω.definition: become sober again, come to one's senses; trans., make sober again, Luc.Bis Acc.17

ἀναξέω.definition: hew smooth, polish, IG7.3073.123 ; part. contr. ib.22.463.72:—Pass., J.AJ13.6.6

ἀναξηραίνω.definition: metaph., consume, exhaust, Call.Cer.114; dry again, after bathing, in Pass., Hp.Acut.65

ἀναπάλλω.definition: poet. Ep. aor. part; an earthquake with an upward movement, Arist.Mu.396a8

ἀναπαύω.definition: poet. and Ion. fut. Med; c. acc. only, put an end to, S.Tr.1262; more freq. rest, make to halt, X.Cyr.7.1.4; Id.HG6.2.29; A.Fr.192 ; E.Hipp.1353; lay it in a reposing posture, Ael.VH12.64, cf. NA7.29: abs., give me re…

ἀναπείρω.definition: poet. pierce through, fix on a; impale, Hdt.4.103:—Pass., Id.4.94; . . Macho ap.Ath.8.349c

ἀναπετάννυμι.definition: or X.An.7.1.17 , poet. Luc.Cal.21: fut. Att. Men.Fr.3 D.:— spread out, unfold, Il.1.480, etc.; E.Hipp.202; unfold, display, Sapph.29; having shed light abroad, E.IA34; throw wide the gates, Hdt.3.146, cf. X.An. l. c.:…

ἀναπηδάω.definition: poet. fut. Luc.Asin.53:—leap; of water, spring, Arist.HA596b18

ἀναπιδύω.definition: spring up, ooze out, Thphr.CP6.4.1; of ground, send forth water, Plu.Aem.14

ἀναπίμπλημι.definition: metaph., accomplish what is destined, as always in Hom., having filled up the full measure of their fate, Il.11.263; 4.170; ib.8.465, 15.132, Od.5.302, 13.307 , cf. Hdt.5.4, 6.12, 9.87, etc

ἀναπλέω.definition: Ion. Ep. , sail; put out to sea, Il.11.22, cf. And.1.76, Decr. ap. D.18.184; IG2.471.28

ἀναπλόω.definition: unfold, open, Mosch.2.60; cause to expand, Anon.in Cat.49.26

ἀναπνέω.definition: Ep. impf. A.R.3.231: Ep. aor; revive, burn up again, Thphr.HP5.9.6

ἀναποδίζω.definition: make to step back, call back and; in no other passage did he correct himself, retract what he before said, Hdt.2.116

ἀναπομπή.definition: sending up, e.g. to the; digging up of treasures, Luc.Alex.5

ἀνάπτω.definition: make fast on or to, Hom; hang up in a temple, offer up, like Od.3.274, cf. Arist.Fr.572, Lyc.853, Philostr.VA1.11, Tryph.256

ἀναπυρόω.definition: set on fire, Arist.Mu.395a22 : intr., metaph., break out afresh, . . Gal.16.742

ἄναρθρος.definition: not differentiated or articulated; without visible joints, like fat men, Hp.Aër.19

ἀνάριθμος.definition: poet. without number; without number, i. e. having no assigned number, Plot.6.6.11

ἀναρπάζω.definition: snatch away, carry off, . . Il.9.564, cf. 16.437, Od.4.515, 5.419; of slave-dealers, kidnapped me, 15.427, cf. X.An.1.3.14, Aristid.1.161 J., etc.; . . E.Hipp.454; of an eagle, Ar.V.17, cf. Epicr.2.10:—Pass., S.El.848…

ἀναρραφή.definition: lifting by sewing up, of the eyelid, Leonid. ap. Aët.7.71

ἀναρρήγνυμι.definition: break through, break open, Il.7.461; E.Hec.1040; Plb.5.71.9; Plu.Pel.12:—Pass., Th.7.34

ἀναρρίπτω.definition: metaph. from dicing, stand the hazard of a thing, run a risk, Hdt.7.50, Th.4.85, 95; Plu.Nic.11; Id.Dem.20; Id.Brut.40: with omitted, throw for one's all, stake one's all, Th.5.103; risk a battle, Plu.Caes.40, etc.; a…

ἀναρροιβδέω.definition: poet. swallow back, suck down again, Od.12.104; ib.105, cf. 236:—Pass., Gal.Sect.Intr.9; but in S.Fr.440, throw up, as expl. by Phot.p.120 R., cf. Paul.Aeg.3.10

ἀνάρροπος.definition: tilted up, like one side of a balance; retrograde, Men.Prot.p.68 D

ἄναρχος.definition: without head or chief, Il.2.703; a year without any regular magistrates, GDI5635

ἀνασάττω.definition: load up, pile up, pf. part. Pass. Plb.12.25h.2; cf. luxatur, Gloss. Philox

ἀνάσεισις.definition: shaking up and down, esp. for the purpose of threatening, Dexipp.p.182 D.; Lib.Or.18.189

ἀνασεύομαι.definition: Pass., only aor., . . the blood sprang forth, spouted up, Il.11.458

ἀνάσσω.definition: impf. Od.11.276, Dor; in Trag. sts. metaph. of things, E.Fr.705; Hel.1040; IT17; lord of the leap, dub. in A.Pers.96; of Persephone, E.Ion1049 :—Pass., is held as lord, S.Ph.140

ἀναστενάχω.definition: c. acc. pers., groan aloud over, bemoan, bewail aloud, ib.23.211:—so in Med., 18.315,355

ἀναστρέφω.definition: poet. pf. v.l. in Theognet.1.8, 3pl. Cerc.Fr.17.30:-turn upside down, . . might upset them, Il.23.436; E.Supp.331; Ar.Av.1240; Cerc.l.c.; upset the stomach, i.e. cause sickness, Th.2.49; reverse, A.Pers.333, Ar.Pl.779…

ἀναστρωφάω.definition: intr. in Act., retire, desist from, Arat.1069

ἀνασύρω.definition: pull up, Procop.Goth.4.11; in Pass. also, of Alexander's hair, to be curly, Ael.VH12.14

ἀνατέλλω.definition: poet. aor. pf. part; bring forth, give birth to ib.7.5; A.R.2.44: of events, S.Ph.1139

ἀνατήκω.definition: melt: metaph., relax, Plu.2.136b:— Pass., of snow, thaw, Plb.2.16.9

ἀνατίθημι.definition: pf. SIG1018.9 , etc.:—lay; in Prose, refer, attribute, a thing to a person, Hdt.2.135; would not have attributed to her the erection of the pyramid, ib.134; E.El.1296; . . will give me the credit of it, Th.2.64; D.18.…

ἀνατομή.definition: dissection, title of a treatise; in a logical sense, Arist.APo.98a2

ἀνατρέπω.definition: poet. Aeol. aor; Medic., upset, Gal.12.911: so abs., create nausea, Aristaenet.1.12

ἀνατρέχω.definition: fut. Luc.Ind.4, poet. 3sg; c. acc., retrace, traverse, Pi.O.8.54, cf. Semon.10; undo, Men.15D.; make amends for, Plu.2.2c, cf. Luc.Ind.4

ἀνάτριχος.definition: with hair bristling backwards, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.13

ἀνατροφή.definition: education, Aphth.Prog.8; rearing; feeding, diet, Porph.Abst.3.17
