ἀναυξία.definition: Ion. defect in growth, Hp.Art.52 ; written in Ath.Med. ap. Orib.inc. 21.1

ἀναφαίνω.definition: bring to light, produce, Hdt.4.105; proclaim, declare, Id.P.4.62; ib.9.73, cf. N.9.12: c. part., Pl.Criti.108c: c. inf., . . I proclaim that they call thee by this name, E.Ba.528:—Med., in Dor. form adopt as one's son…

ἀναφέρω.definition: bring, carry up, Od.11.625; Hdt.4.195, cf. 3.102 ; X.Smp.8.30 , Plu.Rom.28, etc.; in histor. writers, carry up the country, esp. into Central Asia, Hdt.6.30; raise up, Hp.Art.37; lift it, E.Ph.1410:—Med., carry up to …

ἀναφορά.definition: coming up, rising; Astron., ascent of a sign measured in degrees of the equator, Ptol.Tetr.134

ἀναφράζω.definition: relate, describe, Eun.Hist.p.223 D.; Med., to be aware of, Od.19.391

ἀναφύσημα.definition: upward blast, eruption of wind; Medic., powder for inflation, Hippiatr.98

ἀναχάζω.definition: make to recoil, force back, found only in; mostly as Pass., Ep. aor. back, freq. in Il. of warriors, 7.264, cf. 15.728, 16.819, 17.47, etc.; giving way to the wave, Od.7.280: c. gen., draw back from . ., A.R.4.1241; r…

ἀναχαράσσω.definition: Att. scrape up, ib.913e; air causes the roughness of rust, ib.396a, cf. 454c

ἀναχέω.definition: pour forth, Ph.1.50; cause to; metaph., relax, Ph.1.104; is dissipated, dissolved, Dam.Pr.29

ἀναχορεύω.definition: begin a choral dance, Ar.Th.994: and c. acc; celebrate in the chorus, ib.1153

ἀναχωρέω.definition: Locr., Cret. go back; walk backwards, of oxen feeding, Hdt.4.183

ἀναψύχω.definition: Ep. impf. Orph.L.562:—cool; let the ships rest and get dry, Hdt.7.59, X.HG1.5.10; let it dry off, Plu.Sull.29; dry them, Id.Them.30:—Pass., to be dried up, Str.10.2.19

ἁνδάνω.definition: impf. Ep. in Ion; in Hdt. expresses the opinion of a body of people, 7.172, cf. 9.5; 9.19: c. inf., 6.106, cf. 4.145,153, 201; so Il.17.647, cf. Od.2.114:— quae placuerunt, IG9.334

ἀνεγείρω.definition: wake up, rouse, Il.10.138; metaph. also, rouse, encourage, Od.10.172; stir, rouse the spirit of, X.Eq.9.6:—Med., take heart, Ph.2.120

ἀνειλέω.definition: roll up or crowd together; unroll, ib.109d

ἄνειμι.definition: in Att. serving as fut. to and Ep. as impf.:-go up, at sun-rise, Il.18.136, cf. Hdt.3. 85; I went up a hill, Od.10.146, cf. Pl.R.614d; E.Fr.687; came up upon the skin, S.Tr.767: metaph., reach, attain to, Pl.R.531c: M…

ἀνείργω.definition: keep back, restrain, used by Hom. always in; force back, D.H.3.32

ἀνέκφορος.definition: not to be brought to light; Medic., there is a general stoppage , Archig. ap. Aët.9.28

ἀνέλιξις.definition: unfolding: hence, evolution in; unfolding in growth, Simp.in Ph.632.31

ἀνελίσσω.definition: Att. Ep. and Ion. (v; unravel, 'explicate', Procl.in Euc.p.4F., cf. Prisc.Lyd.34.23; explicit definition, Simp.in Ph.276.28

ἀνέλκω.definition: draw up, . . holds them up (in; drag up, drag out, Ar.Pax307; having dragged him into open court, Id.Ach.687; drags them into the witness-box, Id.V.568: —Med., tear one's own hair, Il.22.77:—Pass., D.P.790

ἀνεμώνη.definition: poppy anemone, Anemone coronaria; scarlet wind-flower, Anemone fulgens, ibid.; also called CrateuasFr.4; Thphr.HP6.8.1

ἀνεξιόομαι.definition: to be reduced to a metallic state, Zos.Alch.p.153B

ἀνέξοδος.definition: with no outlet, not to be got out of; unfit for an expedition, Plu.2.269e

ἀνέραμαι.definition: aor. love again, love anew, c. gen., And.1.127, and perh. X.Mem.3.5.7

ἀνέρρω.definition: go quite away, take oneself off, Eup.221

ἀνέρχομαι.definition: of trees, grow up, shoot up, Od.6.163,167; of the sun, rise, A.Ag.658; A.R.3.1230; of water, rise, Arist.Mete.358b32, Heph.Astr.1.23: metaph., E.Or.810

ἀνερωτάω.definition: question, c. acc. pers; c. acc. rei, inquire into, Id.Men.84d,al

ἀνεσθίω.definition: eat away, of ulcers, etc., in Pass., Hp.Epid.4.1, Aret.SD1.13

ἀνέχω.definition: impf. also impf. fut; lift up as an offering, . . 11.10.461; as a testimony, 7.412; of Hecuba entreating her son Hector, 22.80; . . A.R.2.254; A.Fr.126

ἄνεω.definition: Adv. without a sound, in silence, Il.9.30,695; 2.323; 3.84, Od.7.144, 10.71; 2.240.—In all the places cited it is joined with a pl. Verb, and is commonly written

ἀνηβάω.definition: grow young again, Hes.Op.132; grow up, attain to Call.Jov.56

ἀνηγέομαι.definition: Dor. relate, rehearse; intr., advance worthily in the Muses' car, Pi.O.9.80

ἀνήδομαι.definition: renounce one's enjoyment of a thing, no longer enjoy it, Hermipp.77

ἀνηκουστέω.definition: to be unwilling to hear, disobey, c. gen., Il.15.236; A.Pr.40; Th.1.84: c. dat., Hdt.6.14: also abs., 1.115, Aen.Tact.10.3

ἀνήκω.definition: to have come up to a point, reach up to, of; it has come to you to have, has become yours to have, Hdt.6.109

ἀνήνεμος.definition: without wind, without the blast of storms, S.OC677 ; gentle, Olymp.in Mete.201.22

ἀνθέριξ.definition: = beard of an ear of corn; = I.1 , stalk of asphodel, v.l. in Theoc.1.52

ἀνθέω.definition: blossom, bloom, of the youthful beard; of flowers and plants, first in Hes.Op.582, Alc.39; S.Fr.395; flourish, Theoc.27.46: c. dat., h.Ap.139; Pi.I.4.18: metaph., A.Ag.659; dub.l. in Ar.Lys.1257

ἀνθίστημι.definition: set against, Th.4.115; esp. in battle; match with, compare, Plu.Thes.1

ἀνθόβολος.definition: garlanded with flowers, AP9.270 , but codd. have i.e. shedding flowers

ἀνθοκόμος.definition: decked with flowers, flowery; parti-coloured, Opp.C.2.190

ἀνθομοιόω.definition: compare, Philostr.Dial.2:—Pass., to be compared in turn, Iamb.in Nic.p.12P

ἀνθορμέω.definition: lie at anchor opposite, Th.7.19; of two hostile squadrons before fighting, 2.86; 7.34

ἀνθοφορέω.definition: gather honey from flowers, of bees; produce flowers, AP10.16

ἀνθοφόρος.definition: bearing flowers, flowery; flower-bearer, title of a priestess of Demeter and Kore, IG12.526, cf. 609

ἀνθρακόομαι.definition: Pass., to be burnt to cinders or ashes; form a malignant ulcer , Aët.7.2

ἀνθρήνη.definition: hornet, wasp, Ar.Nu.947; in Arist. the name seems to be given to several diff. species, HA628b32,al

ἀνθυπάγω.definition: bring to trial or indict in turn; rejoin, reply, A.D.Pron.53.21, al.:—Pass., Id.Synt.118.1, 121.22

ἀνθυπακούω.definition: listen to in turn; correspond, answer to, Iamb.in Nic.p.21P

ἀνιάζω.definition: only pres. and impf. (exc. aor; intr., to be grieved or distressed, grieving at heart, Od.22.87; was grieving, growing weary, 4.460, cf. A.R.4.1347; he grieves for his goods, Il.18.300; Arat.196. metri gr. in Hom. and…

ἀνιάω.definition: S.Aj.266, etc.: 3sg. impf. ib.273, Pl.Grg.502a: fut. X.An.3.3.19, Ep. Hom.: aor. And.1.50, etc.; Dor. Theoc.2.23: pf. Hld.7.22:-Pass., Od.15.335, etc., Ion. 3pl. opt. Hdt.4.130: 3pl. impf. X.Cyr.6.3.10: fut. Ar.Fr.488…

ἀνιδίω.definition: perspire so that the sweat stands on the surface Id.Ti.74c

ἀνίημι.definition: as if from dub. in; let come up, give access to, X.HG2.4.11; ib.7.2.12

ἀνιμάω.definition: used by early writers only in pres. and impf; seemingly intr. , get up, X.Eq.7.1

ἀνισοτοιχέω.definition: to be out of trim, lean over to one side, metaph. from a ship, Simp.in Epict.p.108D

ἀνίστημι.definition: raise from sleep, wake up, Il.10.32, etc.; Ar.Ec.740; Eup.305: metaph., S.Tr.979

ἀνιχνεύω.definition: track, as a hound, Il.22.192, cf. Arist.HA624a28 , AP5.301 , Porph.Sent.43, Jul.Or.6.183b: generally, trace out, search out, Plu.Caes.69; Lyc.824:—also Epigr.Gr.270

ἀνοίγνυμι.definition: throw open for use, OGI529.11; opened school, Phld.Acad.Ind.p.103M.; shall I open a shop? Astramps.Orac.43p.5H

ἀνοίκισις.definition: shifting people upward and inland, App.Pun.84

ἀνοκωχεύω.definition: Ion. hold back, stay, hinder; keep up the tension of the ropes, keep them taut, Hdt.7.36

ἀνολβία.definition: Ion. the state of an misery, Hes.Op.319

ἄνολβος.definition: poet. Adj. unblest, wretched, luckless; without means, poor, Arat.1073

ἀνομία.definition: Ion. lawlessness, lawless conduct; the negation of law, opp. D.24.152

ἀνομοιόω.definition: make unlike or dissimilar; make even again, PHal.1.100

ἀνορέγω.definition: hand up, of the elephant's use of his trunk, Arist.HA497b28

ἀνόρεκτος.definition: without appetite for; Pass., not desired, of food, Plu.2.664a

ἀνορούω.definition: poet. Verb, used by Hom. only in aor. 1 :—start up, leap up, abs., Il.9.193, Od.3.149, Sapph.Supp.20a.11, etc.; Od.22.23; Il.10.162, etc.; 11.273; so . . . . Helios went swiftly up the sky, Od.3.1; Il.1.248; Pi.O.7.37

ἀνόστιμος.definition: not returning, cut off; not to be retraced, E.HF431

ἄνοστος.definition: unreturning, without return; = foreg. II, Thphr.CP4.13.2

ἄνοχλος.definition: not in the way, not an impediment, Arist.PA663b20

ἀνταείρω.definition: = only in Med., raise one's hands against one, make war upon him, Hdt.3.144,7.101; or without 6.44.7.212; also

ἀντανάγω.definition: lead up against, esp. put ships; raise in opposition, Philostr.VA4.23

ἀντανέχω.definition: hold up in turn or in reply, Polyaen.6.19.2, cf. 1.40.3, Men.Prot.p.72D

ἀνταπέχω.definition: receive in return, Anatolian Studies p.343

ἀνταΰω.definition: sound in turn, answer, Pi.P.4.197, cf. Opp.C.2.78

ἀντάω.definition: c. dat. pers., come opposite to, meet face to face, meet with, ib.6.399; 7.423; so also in Trag., A.Supp.36; S.Tr.902, etc

ἀντεκθέω.definition: rush out on the other side from, Arr.An.1.21.3

ἀντελαύνω.definition: intr., sail against, with a trireme, Plu.Nic.24

ἀντεμβολή.definition: pipe made of pieces fitted into each; substitute, PHolm. 10.11

ἀντέξαρμα.definition: southerly elevation , corresponding to a northerly one, Theol.Ar.25

ἀντεπάγω.definition: lead against: abs. (sc. or the; inflict in return, Aristaenet.2.9

ἀντέχω.definition: or fut. part. (in; c. dat., hold out against, withstand, Hdt.1.175, cf. S.Fr.78; Th.2.49; Id.6.22; Hdn.3.6.10, etc.: c. acc., endure, AP9.299 ; but in Th.8.63 rather belongs to the next signf., hold out as regards the…

ἀντηρετέω.definition: row against or on the opposite side to another, EM112.40

ἀντιάζω.definition: impf. Hdt.1.166 (but; c. acc. pers., encounter, whether as friend or foe, Id.4.118, cf. 2.141, 4.80, etc.; Hdt.1.166, cf. 9.6; . . A.Ag.1557: abs., . . Pi.N.10.20; song shall answer to the pipe, Id.O.10.84

ἀντιάω.definition: Hom. uses pres. only in the Ep. forms; go for the purpose of meeting or receiving

ἀντιβολέω.definition: rarely c. dat. rei, to be present at, Od.11.416; 24.87; cf; c. gen. rei, partake of, have one's share of, Il.4.342; Od.21.306; 4.547; Hes.Op.784, cf. Pi.O.13.30; even Timo59.1

ἀντίδοσις.definition: giving in return; at Athens, a form by which a citizen charged with a or might call upon any other citizen, whom he thought richer than himself, either to exchange properties, or to submit to the charge himself, Lys.3…

ἀντίδοτος.definition: given in lieu of; given as a remedy for, ib.10.118

ἀντίζυγος.definition: put in the opposite scale: hence; vertical cross-pieces, in building, IG22.463

ἀντιθέω.definition: fut. Hdt.5.22:—run against another; run contrary ways, AP9.822

ἀντικλάζω.definition: sound by striking against; c. acc. cogn., sing against one another, Id.Ba.1057

ἀντικόπτω.definition: cut down mutually, D.C.43.37 (nisi; beat back, resist

ἀντικοτέω.definition: · obstrigillo, obtrecto, officio, Gloss.:—also offensio, ib

ἀντιλαβή.definition: thing to hold by, handle; grip, of a dog, Ael.NA8.1

ἀντίξοος.definition: the opposite side of the compass, Placit.2.12.1

ἀντιξύω.definition: scrape in turn, 'claw me, claw thee', Sophr.149, Aristid.2.84J

ἀντιόομαι.definition: fut. al.: aor. Pass; in , c. acc., that ye would meet him in Boeotia

ἀντιτορέω.definition: bore right through, c. gen., Il.5.337: c. acc., having broken it open, ib.10.267, cf. h.Merc.178

ἀντιφερίζω.definition: set oneself against, measure oneself with, . . Il.21.357; Hes.Th.609; Il.21.488; Ar.Eq.813, cf. 818; Pi.P.9.50

ἀντιφέρω.definition: set against, Pl.Erx.395b; Pass., to be borne in a contrary direction to, Arist.Cael.291b2, cf. Ph.215a30; Theo Sm.p.134 H

ἀντίφονος.definition: in revenge for blood; deaths by mutual slaughter, A.Th.893.—Trag. word, but only in lyric passages

ἀντλία.definition: hold of a ship, S.Ph.482; Ar.Eq.434; . . i.e. the coarse food used by seamen, Dionys.Com.2.41

ἀντοικέω.definition: to be :—Pass., Ptol.Geog.1.8.1, cf. Ach.Tat.Intr.Arat.30, Olymp.in Grg.p.541 J

ἀντολίη.definition: collat. poet. form of Androm. ap; as Adj., eastern, . . Nonn.D.25.98

ἄντομαι.definition: only pres. and impf.: :—poet. Verb; meet with favour, greet, Pi.P.2.71

ἀντορέγω.definition: stretch out, present in turn, Them.Or.11.153a

ἀνυπόθετος.definition: not hypothetical, unconditioned; without foundation, ib.358f

ἀνυφαίνω.definition: weave anew, renew that which wears out, Pl.Phd.87d, cf. Olymp.Vit.Pl.p.3W., in Alc.p.198C

ἀνύω.definition: Il.4.56, Ar.Ra.606, Att. or Th.2.75, Pl.R.486c, al.: impf. Hdt.9.66, E.Hec.1167: fut. S.Aj.607, Ar.Ra.649, Ep. 11.11.365: aor. Od.24.71, A.Pers.726, etc.; poet. Pi.P.12.11, A.R.4.413, Ep. Hes.Th.954, Maiist.57 : pf. P…

ἄνω.definition: imper. S.Ichn.70, inf; Pass., come to an end, be finished, mostly of a period of time, night is quickly drawing to a close, Il.10.251; the waning year, Hdt.7.20; A.R.2.494; SIG577.30 ; also . . Il.18.473; Hdt.1.189, 8…

ἀνωδίνω.definition: to be in labour, bring forth, Nonn.D.41.167

ἀνωδυνία.definition: freedom from pain, Protag.9, Plot.1.4.6: in pl., painfree periods, Philagr. ap. Aët.12.20

ἀνωμαλέω.definition: suffer ups and downs of fortune, Nech. ap. Vett.Val.279.28, cf. 65.6, Heph.Astr.2.28

ἀνώμοτος.definition: unsworn, not bound by oath; not sworn to, D.19.204

ἀνωρία.definition: Ion. untimeliness, the bad season of the year for war, opp. Hdt.8.113

ἀνωφερής.definition: borne upwards, ascending, opp; of wine, heady, intoxicating, Ath.1.32c

ἀνωφορέω.definition: bear up, raise, freq. in Eust., esp. in Pass. as 40.36, al.:—Act., 695.54

ἄξενος.definition: Ion. and poet. inhospitable, of; the Axine, afterwds. called the Euxine, Pi.P.4.203, E.Andr.793 ; in full, Id.IT253,341

ἀξιόλογος.definition: worthy of mention, remarkable; of persons, of note, important, Th.2.10, etc

ἄξυλος.definition: with no timber cut from it, an; without wood, Hdt.4.61,185, AP9.89 ; also, without a load of wood, Luc.Asin.32

ἀογκέω.definition: diminish in bulk: hence, weaken an arch or vault, BCH 23.178

ἀοζία.definition: Ion. attendance on a god, service, Epigr.Gr.425

ἀοίδιμος.definition: sung of, famous in song or story; won by song, of the Sphinx's victims, E.El.471

ἀοίκητος.definition: houseless, banish one from home, D.45.70, cf. Luc.Gall.17

ἄοικος.definition: houseless, homeless, Hes.Op.602; a homeless, i.e. miserable, home, S.Ph.534, cf. Nonn.D.17.42

ἀολλίζω.definition: gather together; later of things, gather together, heap up, AP9.649 ; ib.772

ἀοργησία.definition: a defect in the passion of anger, 'lack of gall', Arist.EN1108a8, cf. 1126a3 :—in good sense, Plu., who wrote a treatise cf. Nic.Dam.p.150 D., Andronic.Rhod.p.575 M., Gal.5.30

ἀορτέω.definition: lengthd. form of found only in aor. 1 part. Pass. hung up, suspended, AP7.696

ἀορτήρ.definition: strap to hang anything to; in Od.13.438 knapsack-strap, v

ἀπαγγέλλω.definition: fut. Ion. Simon.5.18: aor. 1; of a messenger, bring tidings, report, Il.9.626, etc., Pi.P.6.18, Hdt.3.25, etc.; A.Ch.266, X.An.6.3.22, etc.; ib.2.4.4, 6.4.25; ib.2.3.4; Pl.Men.71c, cf. Hp.de Arte11, Th.4.122; E.IT642,…

ἀπάγχω.definition: strangle, throttle, Od.19.230; Ar.Pax795, cf. Plu.Mar.27, Luc.Lex.11; chokes me with anger, Ar.V.686:—Med., aor. and Pass., hang oneself, to be hanged, Archil.67, Hdt.2.131, Hp.Aph.2.43, A.Supp.465, And.1.125, Philem.…

ἀπάγω.definition: lead away, carry off; lead away, draw off troops, Hdt.1.164, cf. Th.1.28, al.; Ar.Nu.32

ἀπαείρω.definition: aor. poet. form of depart; trans., remove, Orac. ap.Porph. ap. Eus.PE5.9

ἀπαθέω.definition: to be free from Phld.Lib.p.40 O

ἀπαιρεθέω.definition: Ion. aor. 1 subj. Pass., and Ion. pf. part. Pass., from

ἀπαίρω.definition: lead or carry away, Hdt.8.57; E.El.774; Id.Hel.1520; elliptically , sail away, march away, depart, Hdt.8.60, freq. in Th., X., etc.: c. gen., depart from the land, E.Cyc.131; Id.Tr.944: c. acc. cogn., to set out on an…

ἀπαιτέω.definition: demand back, demand to have returned, esp. of; call down on oneself, Jul.Or.2.59a

ἀπαιτίζω.definition: = demand back, of things forcibly taken away, Od.2.78, cf. Call.Fr.178; simply, demand, Nonn.D.42.382, cf. Opp.H.5.443

ἀπαλέξω.definition: ward off from, c. acc. rei et gen. pers; c. acc. pers. et gen. rei, Od.17.364

ἀπαλθαίνομαι.definition: fut. heal thoroughly, Il.8.419: impf., Q.S.4.404

ἀπαλοάω.definition: poet. thresh out; metaph., bruise, crush, Il.4.522; generally, destroy, Nonn.D.9.320

ἀπαμάω.definition: fut. cut off, Od.21.300, cf. Hes.Th.181; S.Ph.749:— in Med., Thphr.Lap.21; Q.S.13.242:—Pass., Nonn.D.4.413. in Ep.; but in S

ἀπαμείβομαι.definition: fut. aor. X.An.2.5.15: plpf. AP14.2, Nonn.D.8.165:—reply, answer, freq. in Hom., but always with a second more definite Verb, as Il.1.84, al.; 20.199, al.; X. l.c.; Theoc.8.8

ἀπαμέλγω.definition: suck out milk from the breast, Sor.1.105

ἀπαμπίσχω.definition: take off, Ph.2.43:—Med., doff, 1.653; metaph., lay bare, reveal, 2.74, al

ἀπαμύνω.definition: keep off, ward off, with collat. notion; requite, take vengeance on, AP5.6

ἀπαναίνομαι.definition: disown, reject, Il.7.185; Od.10.297; Pi.N.5.60; part. A.Eu.972 ; of a woman, Hp.Mul.2.179; pres. also in Plu.2.132c

ἀπανθέω.definition: finish blooming, Thphr.HP1.13.3, al.; fade; of wine, lose its sweetness, i.e. ripen, Alex.45

ἀπανύω.definition: finish entirely, the ships performed the voyage home, Od.7.326:—Pass., Q.S.5.1

ἀπαράσσω.definition: Att. strike off; knock or sweep off, Hdt.8.90; Th.7.63:—Pass., aor. part. D.H.8.85

ἀπαρέσκω.definition: c. acc. pers., displease, Pl.Tht.202d, Jul.Mis.365d; abs., J.AJ8.14.1

ἀπαρύω.definition: or fut. draw off; metaph., draw off, take off the force of a thing, Epic. ap. Arist.Po.1457b14; exhaust, come to the end of, Plu.2.463c, etc.:—Med., c. gen., skimming the cream of memory, ib.610e:—Pass., aor. part., .…

ἀπάρχω.definition: fut. , lead the way; prob. reign far away from home, of Teucer, Pi.N.4.46

ἀπασχολέω.definition: leave one no leisure, keep him employed; rendering them of none effect, Hdn.7.2.5

ἀπατάω.definition: late Ion. Luc.Syr.D.27 : impf. E.El.938, Ion. Orac. in Ar.Pax1070: fut. aor. Ion. Il.9.344, S.Tr.500 : pf. Id.Ph.929:-Pass., fut. Arist.APr.67a38, cf. Pl.Cra.436b, Aeschin.2.123; also in Med. form Pl.Phdr.262a, X.An.7…

ἀπαυγάζω.definition: flash forth, Hld.3.4; Med., see from far, Call.Del.125,181

ἀπαυλισμός.definition: seems to be used of a moon-stroke or fit caused by sleeping in the moonlight, Poet. de herb.173

ἀπαφίσκω.definition: cheat, beguile, mostly in compos. with and of the simple word Hom. has only Od.11.217: aor. opt. in act. sense, 23.216:—later, APl.4.108 ; Opp.H.3.444; Q.S.3.49, Nonn.D.5.512: aor. 1 ib.8.129, Q.S.13.280, 2sg. 3.502

ἀπειθέω.definition: Att. form of (though even Trag; of a woman, refuse compliance, Aristaenet.2.20

ἀπειλέω.definition: Elean keep away; unroll, roll off, HeroAut.5.5

ἄπειμι.definition: abs., to be away or absent, and of things, to be wanting, i.e. all that are, every one, S.Ant.1109; Id.El.306; of the dead, v.l. in E.Hec.312; the god not being counted, Hdt.6.53:—in 3pl. impf., and are freq. confused…

ἀπείργω.definition: Ion. and Ep. in Hom. also; keep from doing, prevent , c. acc. et inf., S.Aj.70, cf. E.Rh.432, Antiph.126; E.Hel.1559; Pl.Lg.837d:—Pass., to be debarred from doing, Id.Prm.148e

ἀπεκδύομαι.definition: strip off for oneself, despoil, ib.2.15

ἀπεκλανθάνομαι.definition: forget entirely, found only in aor. 2 imper., Od.24.394

ἀπεμέω.definition: Ep. aor. spit up, vomit forth, Il.14.437, Hp.Aff.15, Opp.H.1.560, Arist.Pr.871a21, Ael.NA9.66, Luc.Cont.7, Gal.14.163:—Pass., Arist.Pr.926b26

ἀπεμφαίνω.definition: to be incongruous, inconsistent; display, . . Malch.p.397 D

ἀπεννέπω.definition: Trag. word, also (only lyr; c. acc.rei, deprecate, . . A.Eu.957

ἀπεντάσσω.definition: put back in its place, of the prolapsed uterus, Sor.2.88

ἀπεράω.definition: fut. vomit, disgorge, Archig. ap; of moisture, generally, carry off, Str.1.3.6:—Pass., prob. in Thphr.CP1.17.10

ἀπέρδω.definition: bring to an end, finish, Hdt.4.62

ἀπέρχομαι.definition: with implying departure from one place and arrival at another, Hdt.1.22; And.4.12; Luc.Tim.11; depart homewards, Th.1.92; Archipp.40; . . went back to the place whence he came, Men.481.3: metaph., Pl.Smp.193c

ἀπεσθίω.definition: fut. Ar.Av.26: aor. part; leave off eating, Theopomp. Com.62

ἀπευθύνω.definition: fut. S.Ichn.169:—make straight; in military drill, dress, Ascl.Tact.12.11, etc

ἀπεύχομαι.definition: wish a thing away, wish it may not happen; reject, despise, A.Eu.608

ἀπεχθαίρω.definition: hate utterly, detest, Il.3.415; make utterly hateful, Od.4.105

ἀπεχθάνομαι.definition: causal, language that causes hatred, opp. X.Smp.4.58

ἀπέχθομαι.definition: later form of Theoc.7.45, Lyc.116, AP5.176 , Plu.Marc.22, etc.; for in E.Hipp.1260 is the better reading; and the inf. freq. found in codd. should be written cf

ἀπέχω.definition: c. dat. pers., . . Od.20.263; c.acc. only, keep off or away, Pi.N.7.61; E.Or.1519

ἀπήθημα.definition: that which is filtered off, Asclep. ap. Gal.14.142, Hippiatr.6, 11

ἀπηχέω.definition: sound back, re-echo, Arist.Pr.899a24, 918a35; utter, Arr.Epict.2.17.8

ἀπήχημα.definition: echo: metaph. of sayings repeated; echo, 'ring', Longin.9.2

ἀπιάπτω.definition: tear away, only in tmesi, Q.S.1.9

ἀπιθέω.definition: Ep. form of c. dat., freq. in; fail to persuade, Pi.P.4.36

ἀπινύσσω.definition: lack understanding, Od.5.342, 6.258; of one lying senseless, Il.15.10; cf. Apollon.Lex. s.v

ἀπιπόω.definition: press the juice from anything, Hdt.2.94

ἀπιστέω.definition: fut. Pass. D.S.32.10, but; disbelieve, distrust, Od.13.339; E.Alc.1130; Ar.Ec.775, cf. Th.7.28 , X.Ages.5.6, 8.7:—Pass., was distrusted, i.e. no one could be sure of knowing, Th.7.44; Antipho2.2.7; X.Cyr.7.2.17, cf. H…

ἀπίσχω.definition: = keep off, hold off, Od.11.95; J.BJ1.7.3

ἁπλόω.definition: make single, unfold, spread out; metaph., be simple, M.Ant.4.26:—Pass., to be simplified, Plot.6.7.35; but, to be expanded, Id.3.5.9

ἀπνευστία.definition: holding of the breath, not breathing, Arist.Pr.881b13,961b21

ἀποβαίνω.definition: fut. with Ep. aor. 1; go away, depart, Il.1.428, 5.133, etc.; 24.468; Od.4.657,715; Il.21.298: c. gen., E.Hec.140; X.Eq.Mag.1.16; of death, E.Andr.1022; of hopes, vanish, come to nought, Id.Ba.909

ἀποβλύζω.definition: spirt out, spirt out some wine; intr., flow forth, Philostr.Im.1.9, cf. Procop.Aed.2.2,al

ἀποβουκολέω.definition: lead astray, as cattle; lead away shepherds from the sheep, Chor.p.92B

ἀποβρίζω.definition: go off to sleep, go sound asleep, Od.9.151: aor. imper. Theoc.Ep.19; Call.Epigr.18; Q.S.5.661

ἀπογαιόω.definition: make into land, Heraclit.All.22 : Medic., form a stone, Gal.19.648,672; cf

ἀπογλυφή.definition: place scraped bare, Asclep. Jun. ap. Gal.12.694

ἀπογυιόω.definition: enfeeble, unnerve, Il.6.265, cf. Ath.1.10b; tire out, cj. for Thphr.Char.7.4

ἀπογυμνόω.definition: strip bare, esp. of arms: hence, in Pass; metaph., lay open, reveal, explain, Paus.4.22.4, App.BC1.57; Jul.Mis.357c

ἀποδακρύω.definition: weep much for, lament loudly; weep away one's judgement, be melted to tears contrary to it, Ar.V.983

ἀποδειροτομέω.definition: slaughter by cutting off the head, or cutting the throat, of men, Il.18.336, 23.22, Luc.DMeretr.13.3; Od.11.35; Hes.Th.280

ἀποδιδράσκω.definition: Ion. fut. Ion; c. acc., flee, shun, Hdt.2.182, Ar.Pax234, etc.; Th.1.128; evade, Arist.Pol.1270b35; D.21.165; . . S.Aj.167.—Rare in Trag

ἀποδίδωμι.definition: fut. aor. 1 aor. 2; refer to one, as belonging to his department, Pl.Lg.765b; refer their case to the Council, Isoc.18.6, cf. Lys.22.2, etc

ἀποδοχή.definition: Aeol. receiving back, having; entertainment, reception, J.AJ12.2.12

ἀποδρύπτω.definition: aor. 1 aor. 2 off the skin, lacerate, Il.23.187; . . Od.17.480; Theoc.25.267:—Pass., Od.5.435, cf. 426; AP11.365 :—Med., scrape oneself, grow thin, dub. in Alciphr.3.51

ἀποδύω.definition: in fut. aor. 1 , trans. used by Hom. of stripping armour from the slain

ἀποζάω.definition: live off, enough to live off; live poorly, Luc.Tox.59, Ael.NA16.12, Lib.Or.11.253

ἀποζευγέω.definition: aor. inf. lit. unyoke: metaph., discontinue treatment, Hp.Loc.Hom.12

ἀποζέω.definition: boil till the scum is thrown off; intr., cease boiling or fermenting: metaph., Alex.45.3

ἀπόζω.definition: smell of something, Luc.DMar.1.5; impers., there comes an odour from Arabia, Hdt.3.113, cf. Luc.Cyn.17

ἀπόθεος.definition: far from the gods, godless, S.Fr.267

ἀποθήκη.definition: any place wherein to lay up a thing; refuge, Philist.59

ἀποθλίβω.definition: press or force back, Arist.HA587a22:—in E.Cyc.237 Ruhnken restored

ἀπόθλιψις.definition: squeezing out of one's place, Luc.Jud.Voc.2

ἀποθνήσκω.definition: serving as Pass. of to be put to death, slain, Hdt.1.137, 7.154; esp. by judicial sentence, Lycurg.93, cf. Pl.Ap.29d, 32d,al., Arist.Rh.1397a30

ἀποθρῴσκω.definition: aor. leap off from, Il.2.702; leap up from, rise from, Od.1.58

ἀποικειόω.definition: absorb completely, assimilate; keep apart, HeroSpir.Praef.p.146S. , s.v.l

ἀποικίζω.definition: Att. fut. A.Fr.304.10:—send away; metaph., banish, Ph.2.221:—Pass., Pl.Plt.284e; is not far removed from . ., Chaerem.18

ἀποινάω.definition: demand the fine due from the murderer , Lex ap.D.23.28, cf. 33:—Med., hold to ransom, E.Rh.177, cf. 66

ἀποίχομαι.definition: fut. impf. be gone; abs., to be gone, to have departed, how long he has been gone, Od.4.109; 21.70, cf. 1.253; his absent father, 1.135, cf. E.Hel.1306 ; Id.Heracl.818: imper. begone! Hecat.30 J

ἀποκαίνυμαι.definition: surpass, vanquish, . . in wrestling again he vanquished all, Od.8.127; . . ib.219, cf. A.R.2.783

ἀποκαλέω.definition: recall, esp. from exile, Hdt.3.53; call away or aside, Id.An.7.3.35

ἀποκάμνω.definition: grow quite weary, fail, flag utterly, mostly; c. inf., cease to do, E.Ion135 ; do not hesitate . ., Pl.Cri.45b

ἀποκάμπτω.definition: intr., turn aside, wheel, opp; curved beak, Horap.2.96

ἀποκαπύω.definition: breathe away, aor. 1 in tmesi, she gasped forth her life, Il.22.467, cf. Q.S.6.523

ἀποκαυσμός.definition: burning, Judeich Altertümer von Hierapolis p.142

ἀποκέλλω.definition: get out of the course or track, AB428

ἀποκηδέω.definition: Dor. = to be remiss, Il.23.413; to be faint, Sophr.78

ἀποκινέω.definition: remove or put away from; intr., move off, abscond, Aen.Tact.10.5, Polyaen.1.43.2

ἀποκλάω.definition: break off, Str.10.2.19: aor. 2 part; dress vines, Ar.Fr.109 , q. v.)

ἀπόκληρος.definition: Dor. without lot or share; abs., disinherited, Arist.Top.112b19

ἀπόκλυσις.definition: washing off, flow and ebb, Them.Or.13.167b

ἀπόκνισμα.definition: that which is nipped off, a little bit, Ar.Pax790

ἀποκονίω.definition: said to be an Aetol. word for kick up the dust, i.e. run, dub. in Hygin.Astr.3.11

ἀποκόπτω.definition: cut off, hew off, freq. in Hom., of men's; metaph., A.R.4.1272, cf. Plb.3.63.8; D.S.13.23; decide summarily, Alciphr.1.8; also Plu.Pyrrh.2; exclude from the reckoning, despair of, Phld.Herc.1251.22; reject, exclude, I…

ἀποκοσμέω.definition: restore order by clearing away, clear away; remove from the world, kill, LXX2 Ma.4.38

ἀποκράζω.definition: cry out under, complain of, Simp.in Epict.p.132 D

ἀποκρατέω.definition: exceed all others; trans., control, remedy, Dsc.4.9

ἀποκρίνω.definition: fut. set apart, prob. in; Medic. in Pass., to be distinctly formed, Hp.Prog.23; of the embryo, Arist.HA561a17; bodily secretions, Hp.VM14; Id.Vict.4.89; but all illnesses determined or ended in this alone, Th.2.49; al…

ἀποκρούω.definition: beat off, drive away, from a place or person; knock off, IG3.1417.12:—Pass., a cup with the lip knocked off, Ar.Ach.459

ἀποκρύπτω.definition: used by Hom. only in aor. 1, Ep. impf. Hes.Th.157:-Pass., aor. LXXJb.3.23: fut. ib.Ps.18.6, Gal.UP10.12:-Med., aor.2 Apollod.3.2.1:-hide from, keep hidden from, c. acc. et gen., . . Il.18.465: c. dat. pers., 11.718: c…

ἀποκτείνω.definition: 2 Ep.Cor.3.6, etc.), fut. Ion. Hdt.3.30: aor. 1 Il.: pf. Isoc.12.66, Pl.Ap.38c, X.Ap.29, D.22.2; plpf. 3pl. Id.19.148, Ion. 3sg. Hdt.5.67; later Arist.SE182b19, Parth.24.2, Plu.Tim.16; also Men.344, Arist.Pol.1324b16,…

ἀποκύπτω.definition: stoop away from the wind, Ar.Lys.1003, in pf. but Reiske

ἀποκωλύω.definition: fut. hinder or prevent from a; c. acc. only, keep off, hinder, Orac. ap. Hdt.1.66, cf. Th.3.28

ἀπολάμπω.definition: shine or beam from; reflect light, Epicur.Ep.2p.51U

ἀπολάπτω.definition: lap up like a dog, swallow greedily, Ar.Nu.811

ἀπολείβω.definition: let drip: hence, pour a libation, Hes.Th.793; dropping honey, D.S.17.75; Alciphr.3.21: metaph., Com.Adesp. 39:—Pass., drop or run down from, Od.7.107; Hes.Sc.174

ἀπολείπω.definition: leave behind in the race, distance: generally, surpass, X.Cyr.8.3.25, Lys.2.4; Isoc.4.50:—more freq. in Med. and Pass., v. infr

ἀπολέπω.definition: aor. 2 Pass. Hsch.:—peel, skin; lop off, Il.21.455

ἀπολήγω.definition: leave off, desist from, c. gen; c. part., leave off doing, 11.17.565, Od.19.166; 11.6.149: abs., cease, desist, ib.13.230, 20.99; . Xenoph.6.3; opp. Emp.17.30; of the wind, fall, Theoc.22.19

ἀπολινόω.definition: tie up with a thread, of surgeons, Paul.Aeg.6.5

ἀπολιχμάομαι.definition: lick off, Il.21.123:—later in Act; lick, Longus1.5

ἀπόλλυμι.definition: or (Th.4.25, Pl.R.608e; or talk or bore one to death, S.El.1360, Ar.Nu.892 : hence, alone, in fut. Id.Ach.470; Pherecr.108.20; by his questions, Antiph.222.8, etc

ἀπολογή.definition: selection, or possibly challenging of jurors, OGI484.54

ἀπολούω.definition: c. acc. rei, wash off, Il.14.7:—Med., . . that I may wash the brine from off my shoulders, Od.6.219; of baptism, Act.Ap.22.16

ἀπολυμαίνομαι.definition: Med., cleanse oneself by bathing, esp. from an Il.1.313, 314, A.R.4.702, cf. Paus.8.41.2; Agath.2.7

ἀπολύω.definition: [v. fut. etc.: fut. Pass; set free, release, relieve from, Hdt.2.30; X.Cyr.8.3.47; Pl.R.365a; Id.Phd.65a, cf. 67a; save them from the trouble of measuring, Arist.Pol.1257a40:— Pass., to be set free, Th.1.70, 7.56, etc

ἀπόμαγμα.definition: anything used for wiping or; dirt washed off, S.Fr.34

ἀπομαδάω.definition: of the hair, fall off, Arist.Mir.836a1

ἀπομηνίω.definition: to be very wroth, persevere in wrath; cease from wrath, AB431, Suid

ἀπόμνυμι.definition: c.acc., deny, disown a son on oath, And.1.127:— Med., = Lat. eieravit, solemnly laid it down, Plu.Cic.19

ἀπομόργνυμι.definition: fut. wipe off or away from; wipe clean, . . Il.18.414:—Med., wiped her cheeks, Od.18.200

ἀπομύσσω.definition: Att. wipe the nose, AP11.268; metaph., stop his drivel, Pl.R.343a

ἀπομύω.definition: fut. shut the eyes close: hence, die, Call.Epigr.41

ἀποναίω.definition: remove, send away, used by Hom. only in aor; aor. Med. in trans. sense, sent away her child, E.IT1260 :—Pass., aor. to be taken away, depart from a place, ib.175 ; Id.Med.166

ἀπονέμω.definition: fut. Pl.Phlb.65b:—portion out, impart; part off, divide, of logical division, Pl.Plt.307b:— in Pass., ib.276d,280d

ἀπονέομαι.definition: go away, depart, freq in Hom., only in pres. and impf., always at the end of the line, with the first syll. long, metri gr., Il. l. c., etc.; Od.5.27; Il.3.313, al

ἀπονεύω.definition: bend away from other objects towards one, turn; abs., hang the head, of barley, Thphr.CP3.22.2

ἀπονέω.definition: unload:—Med., throw off a load from, E.Ion875; AB421; . . A.R.1.364

ἀπονίζω.definition: later D.S.4.59, Plu.Phoc.18, and; wash clean, esp. of the hands and feet, I perceived it as I was washing his feet, Od.23.75; Ar.V.608, cf. Men.Georg.60; Pl.Smp.175a:—Med., wash one's body, v.l. in Od.18.179, cf. 172;…

ἀπονίναμαι.definition: Med., fut. Hom.: Ep.aor. 2 without augm. Hom.; 2sg. opt. Il.24.556, 3pl. h.Cer.132, S.El.211 ; inf. A.R.2.196; part. Od.24.30: later aor. I Luc.Am.52, Procl.in Alc.p.89C.:—have the use or enjoyment of a thing, Il.17.2…

ἀπονοστέω.definition: return, come home, Hom. in phrase Il.1.60, al.; Hes.Op.735; Hdt.4.33; Id.3.124, 4.76; Id.1.42, al.; Id.1.82; rare in Trag. and Prose, when he returns from . ., E.IT731; Th.7.87; abs., X.An.3.5.16

ἀποξενόω.definition: drive from house and home: generally; wean, Sor.1.117:—Pass., become disused to, Agathin. ap. Orib.10.7.1

ἀποξέω.definition: wipe, scrape, Herod.Med.l.c; scrape off, Luc.Somn.2; scrape, Aët.15.11

ἀποξύνω.definition: bring to a point, make taper; make sharp and piercing, Plu.TG2

ἀποξύω.definition: fut. = scrape off; metaph., strip off as it were a skin, Il.9.446, cf. NostiFr.6; Luc.Nav.45; v.l. in Id.Vit.Auct.10: so in Pass., Alciphr.3.40:—Med., scrape off, D.Chr.32.44

ἀποπαπταίνω.definition: look about one, look round, as if to flee, Ion. fut. Il.14.101

ἀποπάσχω.definition: opp. a Stoic term, reject an impression, Arr.Epict.1.28.3

ἀποπαύω.definition: stop or hinder from, make to cease from; c. acc., stop, check, . . Il.18.267; 19.119, al.; so Thgn.829; E.Ba.381 ; Pl.Tht.151a, etc

ἀποπέμπω.definition: send off or away, dispatch, dismiss; of things, send back, Od.17.76; Hes.Op.87

ἀποπέτομαι.definition: fut. Ar.Pax1126: aor. part. inf. Hdt.7.13: also Ar.Av.90; aor.2 3pl. Emp.2.4; inf. AP5.211 :— fly off or away, esp. of dreams, Il.2.71; Od.11.222; Ar.Av.90; ib.1369; Pl.Smp.183e; Arist.HA619a32; IG 9.883.6

ἀποπήσσω.definition: late form for benumb, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.45

ἀποπίεσμα.definition: pressure outwards or off, used of rods slightly bent, Hp.Fract.30

ἀποπίπτω.definition: fall off from, Od.24.7; miss or fail in obtaining, Plb.9.7.1; Procl.Inst.13; fail to record, let slip, D.S.13.84: abs., to be disappointed, fail, Plb.4.36.5, UPZ70.27

ἀποπιστεύω.definition: trust mistakenly; confide strongly in, Procl.in Prm.p.480S

ἀποπλάζω.definition: lead away from, A.R.1.1220, cf. Hsch.:—Pass., only aor., stray away from, Od.15.382; 9.259; . . glancing off the hauberk, Il.13.592; Theoc.22.35; Il.22.291: abs., wander, Od.8.573; to be separated, Emp.22.3; a helm st…

ἀποπλέκω.definition: separate, Pass., Zos.Alch.p.110B.: esp. in pf. part. divorced, separated, PGen.19.3 ; BGU118ii11

ἀποπλέω.definition: Ep. Ion. v.l. in Hdt.4.156,157, cf. Arr.Ind.26.9: fut. Hdt.4.147; Pl.Hp.Mi.371b:— sail away, sail off, Il.9.418, etc.; Hdt.1.1, cf. Ar.Ra.1480; Hdt.4.156; Th.6.61; Id.1.55

ἀποπλήσσω.definition: Att. cripple by a stroke; Med., push off from oneself, Arist.Pr.899b24

ἀποπλύνω.definition: fut. wash well, wash away; wash away, Arist.Sens.443b7

ἀποπνέω.definition: causal in Pi.N.1.47 made them give up the ghost; breathe hard, take breath, Arist.HA587a5; exhale, evaporate, Plu.2.560c

ἀποπνοή.definition: exhalation, evaporation, Arist.Pr.863a7; breeze blowing from a place, Arist.Pr.943b12

ἀποπροαιρέω.definition: take away from, having taken some of the bread to give it away, Od.17.457

ἀποπροτέμνω.definition: cut off from, after he had cut a slice from the chine, Od.8.475, cf. Nic.Th.572

ἀποπτάω.definition: roast sufficiently, Sor.1.51, Lyd.[Mens.]p.182 W.; of ores, smelt, in Pass., Ph.Bel.70.4 and 6

ἀποπτοέω.definition: poet. scare or drive away, Call.Fr.anon.93:— Pass., to be startled, to shy, of horses, Plb.3.53.10

ἀποπτύω.definition: spit out, Il.23.781; of the; abominate, spurn, Hes.Op.726; A.Eu.303; Id.Ag.1192, cf. Pr.1070 , Ar.Pax528, E.Andr.607; disown, A.Ch.197:—aor. freq. used in pres. sense, E.Hel.664, cf.IA874: freq. abs., omen absit, Id.H…

ἀπόρημα.definition: matter of doubt, question, puzzle; esp. in the Dialectic of Arist., objection raised to an , Id.Top.162a17

ἀπορούω.definition: dart away, Il.5.20, etc.; esp. start back, Od.22.95; Orph.A.705. 2. spring up from, Pi.Fr.88

ἀπορραίω.definition: bereave one of a thing, c. dupl. acc., Od.1.404; bereave him of life, 16.428; Emp.128: c. gen. rei, Hes.Th.393

ἀπορρήγνυμι.definition: causal, let one's rage burst forth, D.H.Rh.9.5, cf. Luc.Am.43; burst out with a remark, App.BC2.81: —Pass., . . Id.Syr.15

ἀπορριγέω.definition: 2 pf. shrink shivering from a thing: generally, shrink from doing it, c. inf., Od.2.52

ἀπορρίπτω.definition: poet. Pi.P.6.37, later; cast forth from one's country, A.Ch.914; S.Aj.1019; outcasts, D.18.48, cf. D.H.9.10; of things, reject, PBaden19.12 ; Hdn.4.12.2

ἀπορροή.definition: flowing off, stream; falling of a river, Aristid.Or.36.36

ἀποσεύω.definition: chase away, Nic.Th.77, AP9.642 :—Pass., run away, flee,Hom. only in syncop.aor. 2 Il.6.390, etc.; B.10.82: also aor. Hes.Th.183; haemorrhage, v.l. for in Hp.Acut.29:— Med., = Act., A.R.1.805

ἀποσήθω.definition: sift off, separate by sifting, Dsc.5.88; metaph., riddle completely, rob, Herodic. ap. Ath.13.591c

ἀποσιγάω.definition: keep silent about, make no mention of, c. acc., Demetr.Eloc.149, Ps.-Plu.Vit.Hom.213

ἀποσιτέω.definition: cease to eat, starve, Luc.Asin.33; lose appetite, Orib.inc.6.25

ἀποσιτία.definition: aversion to food, want of appetite; fasting, Porph.Abst.1.27

ἀποσκεδάννυμι.definition: or fut. contr. S.OT138 :—scatter abroad, disperse, Il.19.309; Od.11.385; 8.149; S.l.c.; Epigr. ap. D.18.289:—Pass., to be scattered, Hdt.7.91; straggle away from, X.An.4.4.9; Id.HG5.4.42: —Med., repel and scatter, Pl.…

ἀποσκηνόω.definition: keep apart from; remove one's habitation, LXXGe.13.18

ἀποσκιάζω.definition: cast a shade or shadow; cloud over, dull the brightness of metallic surfaces, Zos.Alch.p.223 B

ἀποσκίασμα.definition: shadow, a shadow cast; illusion, deceit, Men. Prot.p.118 D

ἀποσπάω.definition: fut. tear or drag away from; drag away by the hair, A.Supp.909

ἀποσπένδω.definition: pour out wine, as a drink-offering, at sacrifices, Od.3.394; 14.331; E.Ion1198, cf. Antipho1.20; Pl.Phd.117b:—Pass., AP5.54

ἀποσποδέω.definition: wear quite off, walk one's toes

ἀποστασία.definition: late form for defection; departure, disappearance, Olymp.in Mete.320.2

ἀποστατήρ.definition: one who has power to dissolve an assembly, or to decide a question, Lex Lyc. ap. Plu.Lyc.6; cf

ἀποστείχω.definition: aor. go away, go home, Od.11.132, etc.; imper. Il.1.522: aor. part. Hdt.9.56; A.Supp.769, cf. S.El.799, etc

ἀπόστημα.definition: distance, interval; degree of descent from an ancestor, Arist.EN1100a26

ἀποστίζω.definition: mark with points or lines, f.l. for in Gal.17.560, al

ἀποστίλβω.definition: Ep. impf. Epic. in; abs., phosphorescent, Arist.Mete.370a14; shine brightly, Thphr.Sign.26, Agatharch.95, Luc.DMar.14.2, etc.; Alciphr.1.1

ἀποστρέφω.definition: Dor. aor. SIG 244 ii 16; turn away or aside, divert, v.l. in Th.4.80, etc.; cut off water from a besieged town, Ph.Bel.97.4; SIG 839.14 ; Arr.An.2.1.1; avert a danger, an evil, etc., A.Ag.850 ; prevent, Dsc.2.136; reb…

ἀποστυφελίζω.definition: drive away by force from, Il.18.158, AP7.603

ἀποστύφω.definition: draw up, contract, of the effect of; of preparing tissues for dyes, mordant, PHolm.9.14

ἀποσφάλλω.definition: aor. 1 :—lead astray; cause to err, Lib.Or.59.147

ἀποσχάζω.definition: stronger form of open a vein; scarify, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.18.2

ἀποτάσσω.definition: Att. set apart, assign specially; appoint, settle definitely, Arist.HA585b36

ἀποτέμνω.definition: Ep., Ion., and Dor. fut; cut off, divide, sever, in a geographical sense, . . Hdt.1.72; Id.4.25: mathematically, . . Pl.Men.85a, cf. Arist.Mech.849a37:—Med., Pl.Phlb.42b:—Pass., of troops, to be cut off from the main …

ἀποτίθημι.definition: put away, stow away; expose a child, Pl.Tht.161a

ἀποτιμάω.definition: fail to honour, slight, h.Merc.35; Pass., to be disfranchised, Phleg.Olymp.Fr.14

ἀποτίνω.definition: pay for a thing, . . ib.13.193; . . may atone for making a prey of Patroclus, Il.18.93; made atonement with a great price, ib.4.161; A.Ag.1338 ; S.Ant.1352

ἀποτμήγω.definition: Ep. for cut off from; cut off, sever, 11.146; Hes.Th.188; plough the hill-sides, Il.16.390:— Pass., A.R.4.1052: c. gen., Dam.Pr.34

ἀποτρέπω.definition: c. acc. pers. only, turn away or back, Il.15.276: c. dat. modi, 20.256, cf. 109; deter them, Pl.Chrm.173c; opp. D.21.37; opp. Arist.Rh.1391b33, etc

ἀποτρέχω.definition: fut. Ar.Nu.1005, but; run hard, of one training for a race, Ar. l.c

ἀποτριβή.definition: rubbing away, wearing out, depreciation, D.50.28; damage, = ne quid detrimenti res publica caperet, D.C.37.31

ἀποτρίβω.definition: fut. strengthd. for wear; rub clean, rub down a horse, X.Eq.6.2:—Med., Plu.2.1044b

ἀποτρωπάω.definition: Frequentat. of Il.20.119: abs., Od.16.405. B. Med., c. inf., Il.18.585: c.gen., Od.21.112, etc.: c. acc., A.R.3.16

ἀποτύπτω.definition: incise, open, Hp.Morb.2.55; Med., cease to beat oneself, cease mourning, Hdt.2.40

ἀποφέρω.definition: Hom. only in fut. (Dor; exhale, evaporate, Anon.Lond.22.25:—Pass., to be wafted, Plu.2.681a

ἀπόφημι.definition: fut. aor. 1 Pl.Tht.166a; say no, S.OC317, etc

ἀποφθείρω.definition: fut. destroy utterly, ruin; have an abortion, miscarry, Hp.Epid.1.16

ἀποφθινύθω.definition: poet. Verb, perish; causal, make to perish, lose their life, Il.16.540

ἀποφθίνω.definition: intr. in pres., perish utterly, die away, A.Ag.857; S.Ph.457: also in pf. Them.Or.28.341d: but mostly

ἀποφρύγω.definition: dry up, Eun. ap; aor. 2 Pass. cool down, Maria ap. Zos.Alch.p.238B

ἀποχάζομαι.definition: withdraw from, Od.11.05; APl.4.181 : abs., Hsch.:—Act., only in aor. imper. Id

ἀπόψηκτος.definition: wiped clean: hence metaph., keen- witted, sharp, S.Ichn.363

ἀπόψυξις.definition: cooling, evaporation; shivering fit, rigor, Simp.in Epict.p.50 D

ἀποψύχω.definition: c. acc., breathed out life, S.Aj.1031; AP12.72 : abs., expire, die, Th.1.134, cf. LXX4 Ma.15.17, D.C.43.11,al.; faintly breathing out his life, Bion1.9:—also Pass., Hp.Morb.1.19: aor. 2 A.Fr.104

ἀποψωλέω.definition: sens. obsc., praeputium retrahere alicui, Ar.Ach.592; a lewd fellow, ib.161

ἀπραγέω.definition: do nothing, remain quiet; fare ill, Pittac. ap. Stob.3.1.172

ἀπρεπής.definition: unseemly, unbecoming; of persons, disreputable, indecent, Theoc.5.40

ἀπρόσοδος.definition: without approach, inaccessible; not yielding a return, unproductive, Phld.Oec.p.35J

ἅπτω.definition: fut. aor. pf. Ion; join, A.Eu.307; fasten a contest in wrestling on one, engage with one, Id.Ch.868: —Pass., Arist.Pol.1280b14

ἄπυκνος.definition: not dense, not compressed; in Music, of notes, not included in the , Cleonid.Harm.4, etc

ἀπωθέω.definition: fut. inf. Il.13.367: aor; drive away, Il.17.649; of the wind, beat from one's course, Od.9.81

ἀπώρωτος.definition: not forming a callus, of fractured bones, Dsc.1.70

ἄπωσις.definition: thrusting or driving away; repulsion, opp. Arist.Ph.243a19

ἀπώστης.definition: one that drives away, Eust.1741.22; cf

ἀπωτέρω.definition: Comp. Adv. of farther off, S.OT137; c. gen., farther from, Cratin.229

ἀραβέω.definition: rattle, ring, Hom. (mostly in; trans., gnash, grind, Hes.Sc.249, A.R.2.281

ἀραίωσις.definition: becoming or making porous; Medic., porosity, of the lungs, Hp.Oss.13, etc

ἀράομαι.definition: Aeol. inf. Sapph.Supp.5.22: fut; c. acc. et inf., pray that . . , 11.9.240; . . Hdt.3.65 codd.; prayed that they might prevail, 8.94; . . S.Aj.509, cf. Ar.Th.350

ἀραρίσκω.definition: fit together, construct, Il.16.212:—Med., Hes.Sc.320; having prepared, contrived, Od.16.169

ἀράσσω.definition: Att. Ion. and poet. impf; c. dat. modi, assail with reproaches or threats, S.Aj.725, Ph.374, cf

ἀργύρωμα.definition: silver plate, mostly in pl; imitation silver, an alloy of tin, copper, and silver, PHolm.1.35

ἀρέσκω.definition: impf. Th.5.37, etc.: fut; of pers. only, make good, make amends, Il.9.120:—Med., 4.362, cf. Od.22.55, Q.S.4.377, 9.510; make full drink-offerings to the gods, Thgn. l.c

ἀρετάω.definition: thrive, prosper; choose the path of valour, Procop.Goth.4.35, cf. Aed.1Prooem

ἀρετόομαι.definition: Pass., become excellent, grow in goodness, Simp.in Epict.p.10D., Id.in Ph.1066.5

ἀρήγω.definition: fut. Com.Adesp.12.5D., etc.:—aid; impers., c. inf., it is good or fit, Pi.P.2.94; A.Eu.571

ἀρητήρ.definition: one that prays: poet. for , priest, Il.1.11, 5.78, al.; also in metr. Inscrr., IG4.1007 , 1538 , etc., cf. Orac. ap. Jul.Ep.89

ἀρθμέω.definition: intr., to be united, Il.7.302:—Pass., A.R.1.1344

ἀρθρόω.definition: fasten by a joint:—Pass., to be; mostly of words, utter distinctly, produces articulate sounds, X.Mem.1.4.12 ; of persons, render articulate, . . . . Nic.Dam.p.65 D

ἀρθρωδία.definition: a particular kind of articulation, where the surfaces are only slightly concave and convex, ib.736

ἀριθμέω.definition: impf. as trisyll., Od.10.204; count out, pay, X.Smp.4.44, D.49.30, IG 5.1390.51 , Mon.Anc.Gr.7.22

ἀριστεύω.definition: to be best or bravest; c. inf., he was best at fighting, Il.16.292,551, etc.; v. supr

ἀριστητής.definition: one who breakfasts, i.e. takes more than one full meal in the day, Hp.Aër.1

ἀριφραδής.definition: clear, manifest; clear to the sight, bright, Id.24.39

ἀρκέω.definition: c. dat. only, defend, Il.15.529; without dat., 13.371; c. acc. cogn., make good, achieve, S.Aj.439

ἁρμόζω.definition: Att. Dor. Theoc.1.53; generally, adapt, accommodate, award each his just due, Sol.36.17; accord them life, Pi.N.7.98; apply a remedy, S.Tr.687; make ready, Hegesipp.Com.1.19:—Med., accommodate, suit oneself, Philem.l.…

ἁρμοστής.definition: one who arranges or governs, esp; title of officials at Thessalonica, IG11.1053

ἀρνέομαι.definition: refuse, . . Od.21.345, cf. Hes.Op.408, Hdt.3.1; Od.1.249; decline, renounce a duty or office, D.18.282; Id.36.34; PFlor.61.49 ; of a suicide, AP7.473 ; S.E.M.11.163; cast aside humanity, Him.Or.2.10

ἄρνυμαι.definition: imper. Sapph.75, Trag.Adesp.4: fut. Pi.P.1.75, Att. S.OC460, Aj.75, Pl.Lg.969a: aor. 2 Il.11.625, 23.592 ; subj. Hes.Op.632, Il.12.435; opt. 18.121, S.El.34, etc.; inf. Il.16.88, S.Aj.246 ; part. A.Eu.168 :-win, gain,…

ἀρόσιμος.definition: arable, fruitful, corn-; metaph., fit for engendering children, S.Ant.569

ἀρόω.definition: pres. inf. Hes.Op.22: fut; sow, Pl.Phdr.276b:—metaph. in Pass., . . S.Fr.320

ἁρπάγη.definition: hook for drawing up buckets, etc., Men.829

ἁρπάζω.definition: fut. Il.22.310, Babr.89.2; seize hastily, snatch up, Il.12.445; A.Th.624; X.An.6.1.8; seize him by the waist, Hdt.9.107; of the magnet, Hp.Steril.243: c. gen. of the part seized, E.Cyc.400: c. gen. partit., Timocl.16.…

ἁρπαλίζω.definition: catch up, be eager to receive; exact greedily, A.Eu.983

ἄρριγος.definition: insensible to cold, Arist.Sens.438a22; without shivering, Aret.SD1.14

ἀρτεμέω.definition: to be safe and sound, Nonn.D.35.387

ἀρτέμων.definition: foresail of a ship; principal pulley in a system, Vitr. 10.2.9

ἀρτίδορος.definition: just stript off or peeled, cj. Toup in AP6.22 for

ἀρτιπαγής.definition: just put together or made; freshly coagulated, AP9.412

ἀρτίπαις.definition: lately a boy, prob. f. l. for Thom.Mag. s.v

ἀρτιφανής.definition: just seen, having newly appeared, ib.12.5,al

ἀρτόμελι.definition: plaster or poultice of bread and honey, Gal.10.692, Aët.3.177

ἀρτόπονος.definition: one who bakes loaves for Apollo Maleatas, IG4.1549

ἀρτύνω.definition: fut. Ion. Od.1.277: aor. Act. Med. Pass. = chiefly used in Ep. , Od.11.366; 14.469; 24.153; Il.15.303; 11.216; Od.1.277; putting themselves in order, dressing their ranks, Il.12.43, cf. 86, 13.152:—Med., prepared his …

ἀρτυτήρ.definition: director, official of a college at Thera, Test.Epict.4.37, al

ἀρτύω.definition: Od.4.771, impf. Hom. , the only; in culinary sense, dress savoury meat, season, S.Fr.1122, Cratin.303; Arist.EN1118a29:—Pass., . . Pherecr.108.23; Eup.335; Hp.VM14; Thphr.Od.51

ἀρχαΐζω.definition: to be old-fashioned, copy the ancients in manners, language, etc., D.H.Rh.10.7, Plu.2.558a

ἀρχεύω.definition: command, c. dat; to be chief magistrate or official, OGI 166.3 , cf. SIG1023.87

ἀρχιζάπφης.definition: or title of religious official at Delos, Roussel Délos Colonie Athénienne416

ἀρχιφύλαξ.definition: commandant of guards, in; title of an official of the Lycian league, TAM2.199

ἄρχω.definition: Ep. inf. Il.20.154: impf; in Time, begin, make a beginning, Act. and Med. , to be the aggressor, Th.1.53; to begin one's operations, X.HG6.3.6; to open a conversation, Id.An.1.6.6; to begin one's speech, ib.3.2.7. Constr

ἄσαρκος.definition: without flesh, lean, opp; not consisting in flesh, Epicur.Fr.464; Porph.Abst.1.1

ἀσαφής.definition: indistinct , dim, faint; of persons, obscure, Pl.R.392d

ἀσάω.definition: Thgn.593; elsewh. Pass. imper. part. aor. : :—orig. glut oneself, take a surfeit, and so perh. in Sapph.Supp.2.7; but usu., feel loathing or nausea, caused by surfeit, Hp.Morb.Sacr.25, Int.35; of pregnant women, Arist…

ἀσέλγεια.definition: licentiousness, wanton violence; licentiousness, Plb.36.15.4, etc

ἀσελγής.definition: licentious, wanton, brutal, And.4.40; lascivious, lewd, Jul.Caes.315c

ἀσθενής.definition: without strength, weak; in body, feeble, sickly, Hdt.4.135, cf. Hp.VM12; Pi.P.1.55, etc.; D.21.165; Luc.Nigr.4; least able to bear hardship, Hdt.4.134; too weak to . . , D.23.54. Adv. Pl.Lg.659e, cf. OGI751.8

ἀσθμαίνω.definition: breathe hard: used by Hom. in pres. part., panting, as after running, Il.10.376; gasping for breath, of one dying, . . 5.585, cf. 10.496, Pi.N.3.48: pres. ind., Hp.Morb.3.7, Arist.Pr.905b33: impf., Luc.DMeretr.5.4; wi…

ἀσιτέω.definition: abstain from food, fast, E.Hipp.277; have no appetite, Hp.Aph.2.32

ἀσιτία.definition: Ion. want of food, Hdt.3.52; abstinence from food, Hp.Acut.34, Arist.EN1180b9

ἄσιτος.definition: without food, fasting, Od.4.788; of forbidden food, Ph.2.398

ἀσκέω.definition: work raw materials, Il.3.388,4.110; of personal adornment, dress out, trick out, Hdt.3.1; decks herself, E.El.1073; Id.Tr.1023:—freq. in Pass., furnished with.., Emp.61.4; A.Pers.182; S.El.452; of buildings, Hdt.2.169…

ἄσκησις.definition: exercise, practice, training; generally, mode of life, profession, Luc.Vit.Auct.7; of a philosophical sect, Id.Tox.27

ἀσκητής.definition: one who practises any art or trade; hermit or monk, Ph.1.643

ἀσκήτρια.definition: fem. of II, Cat.Cod.Astr.7.225.29, cf. Anatolian Studies p.81

ἀσκιαστόω.definition: clear from rust, Zos.Alch.p.183 B.:—hence ib.217 B

ἀσκοδορέω.definition: flay a person and make a bag of his skin, Ps.-Callisth.3.8

ἀσκοφορέω.definition: bear wineskins at the feast of Bacchus, AB214:— Adj. ibid

ἀσμενέω.definition: = only in Din.1.34 wish for a change

ἀσπάζομαι.definition: Ep. aor. Epigr.Gr.990.9:—welcome; take leave of, Id.Tr.1276; take a last farewell, Lys.13.39

ἀσπαίρω.definition: impf. Ion. and Ep. Q.S.11.104: :—pant, gasp, struggle, in Hom. always of the dying , ib.571; 12.203, cf. Od.19.229, A.Pers.977 , E.IA1587; Antipho2.4.5; E.El.843; of an infant, Hdt.1.111; of fish taken out of the wate…

ἄσπασμα.definition: = sq., esp. in pl., embraces; thing embraced, dear one, Plu.2.608e

ἄσπονδος.definition: without or drink-offering: hence; of a god, to whom no drink-offering is poured, i.e. death, E.Alc.424

ἀστατέω.definition: to be never at rest; to be unsettled, to be a wanderer, 1 Ep.Cor.4.11; to be inconstant, Vett.Val.116.30

ἀστοχία.definition: missing the mark, failing, Phld.Vit.p.41; imprudence, thoughtlessness, error, Plb.2.33.8, etc

ἀστράβη.definition: mule's saddle, an easy padded saddle; a kind of surgical appliance, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.4.34

ἀστράπτω.definition: impers., it lightens, it lightened, S.Fr.578, cf. Arist.Rh.1392b27

ἀσύμβατος.definition: Att. not coming to terms; not comparable, disparate: incongruous in other respects, Gal.5.540

ἀσυμπαθής.definition: without fellow-feeling or sympathy; Medic., unaffected by an operation, Sor.2.60

ἀσύμποτος.definition: made of non-absorbent material, Afric. ap. Olymp.Alch.p.75 B

ἀσυνεχής.definition: not continuous; of winds, variable, Thphr.Vent.11

ἄσφυκτος.definition: without pulsation, lifeless; Act., causing no violent pulsation, ib.132e

ἀσφυξία.definition: stopping of the pulse, Aret.SA2.11; pulsus amputatio, opp. Cael.Aur.TP4.3

ἀσχαλάω.definition: only pres. , 3 sg. Il.2.293; 3pl. 24.403; inf. 2.297; part. 22.412; imper. Archil.66.6; inf. E.IA920:—more freq. once in Hom. Od.2.193, cf. S.OT937, E.Or.785, and so always in Prose, X.Eq.10.6, D.21.125, Onos.1.17, Eu…

ἀσώματος.definition: disembodied, incorporeal, Pl.Phd.85e; non-metallic, Maria ap.Zos.Alch.p.196B

ἀσωτεύω.definition: lead a profligate, spendthrift life; c. acc., squander in riotous living, Ael.VH5.9

ἄτακτος.definition: not in battle-order, of troops, Hdt.6.93; not at one's post, Lycurg.39

ἀτάλλω.definition: only in pres. and impf., skip in; Act., bring up a child, rear, foster, Hom.Epigr.4.2; S.Aj.559: metaph., Pi.Fr.214:—Pass., grow up, wax, h.Merc.400:—Act., intr. in this sense, Hes.Op.131.—Poet. and later Prose

ἀτασθάλλω.definition: to be insolent, only in pres. part., . . Od.18.57; . . 19.88

ἄτεκνος.definition: without children, childless, barren; in causal sense, A.Eu.785. S. l. c., A. and E. ll.cc.]

ἀτέμβω.definition: only pres., maltreat; Med. like Act., Q.S.5.147, 173: c. dat., blame, be dissatisfied with, A.R.2.56, 3.99: c. inf., Id.2.1199

ἀτενίζω.definition: look intently, gaze earnestly; metaph. of the mind, Arist.Ph.192a15; Phld.Ir.p.96 W.; to be obstinate, Lync. ap. Ath.7.313f

ἀτευκτέω.definition: fail in gaining; Pass., to be unsuccessful, of an operation, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.25.6

ἀτέω.definition: part. demented, reckless, c. gen., defying the gods, Il.20.332 ; Call.Fr.537: abs., Hdt.7.223

ἀτίζω.definition: mostly in pres. part.; 2 and 3 sg., E.Rh.327, 253 ; inf., S.OC1153: fut. A.Fr.105: aor. subj. Id.Eu.542 ; Ep.aor. A.R.1.615:—Pass., Gal.18.642:— not to honour, not to heed, unheeding, Il.20.166: c.acc., slight, treat …

ἀτιμάζω.definition: c. gen. rei, treat as unworthy of, A.Pr.783; = S.OC49, cf. Ant.22

ἀτιμάω.definition: Ep. impf. fut. aor. pf. Gal.1.10:—Pass., aor. Id.5.44:—used by Hom. for dishonour, disdain, Od.16.307; 21.99; 23.28; Il.1.11, cf. 94, al.; 8.163, cf. Hes.Op.185; used once by Pi. in Dor. aor. P.9.80; once by S. in imp…

ἀτιτάλλω.definition: metaph., cherish, Theoc.17.58: c. dat., Id.15.111; in bad sense, beguile, cajole, Hippon.86.— Poet. and late Prose, as Them.Or.20.234b

ἀτλητέω.definition: to be impatient, not to endure or submit to a thing, S.OT515

ἀτμεύω.definition: for to be a slave, Nic.Al.172

ἀτμίζω.definition: pf. Arist.Pr.930b36:—smoke; to be vaporized, ib.349b23,358b16,al

ἀτμίς.definition: sublimate or deposit of colouring matter, PHolm.4.21; poultice, Crito ap. Gal.13.879

ἀτοκέω.definition: not to bring forth, to be barren, Ph.1.478

ἀτομόω.definition: leave undivided, Olymp.in Alc.p.181 C.:—Pass., to be individualized, Simp.in Ph.255.28; to be unified, Id.in de An.217.36

ἄτοξος.definition: without bow or arrow, Luc.D Deor.19.1

ἄτριστος.definition: not crackling, i.e. stiff, of tin, Zos.Alch.p.161 B.:—hence make stiff, Id.p.162B

ἀτροφία.definition: want of food or nourishment, of trees; atrophy, Arist.Pr.888a10, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.21.7

ἄτυμβος.definition: without burial, without a tomb, Luc.Cont.22. Adv. prob. in Anatolian Studies p.118

ἄτυπος.definition: speaking inarticulately, stammering; conforming to no distinct type , Gal.7.471

ἀτυχής.definition: unfortunate, Antipho2.2.1; missing, without share in, Ael.NA11.31, Max.Tyr.20.5

αὐαίνω.definition: wither, Thphr.HP3.7.1 : metaph., Sol.4.36; A.Ch.260; I shall waste life away, pine away, S.El.819: I shall wither away, Id.Ph.954; Ar.Fr.613

αὐγάζω.definition: fut. aor. AP7.726 :—Pass; of the sun, illumine, E.Hec.637 :—Pass., Id.Ba.596

αὐδάω.definition: utter sounds, speak, Il.1.92, etc.; 5.786; . . 17.420; utter a cry, E.Ion893

αὐερύω.definition: i. e. Ep. for = Att; of leeches, suck, Opp.H.2.603

αὐθήμερος.definition: made or done on the very day; curing in one day, Gal.12.755

αὐλίζομαι.definition: aor. 1 always in Th., as 4.13; Act., cause to dwell, ib.Je.38.9, D.Chr.35.16

αὔξη.definition: = dub. l. in Hp.Nat.Puer.16, the; dimension, Id.R.528b

αὐτερέτης.definition: one who rows himself, i.e. rower and; rowing one's own boat, AP7.305

αὐτογῆ.definition: ideal earth, archetype of earth, Plot.6.7.11, Herm. ap. Stob.3.11.31

αὐτογνῶσις.definition: absolute knowledge, Olymp.in Phd.p.100 N., Procl.in Alc.p.88C

αὐτόγυος.definition: a plough whose is of one piece with the and not fitted together , Hes.Op.433, A.R.3.232, 1285

αὐτοδυάς.definition: the ideal number two, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.87.9, Phlp.in de An.77.8

αὐτοεῖδος.definition: abstract form, read by Alex.Aphr. in Arist.Metaph.1087a6

αὐτοέν.definition: abstract unity, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.87.9, al., Plot.5.3.12, 6.2.5, Procl.in Prm.p.547 S., Inst.2, al

αὐτοηδύ.definition: pleasure in the abstract, v.l. in Arist.Top.147a8

αὐτόθεος.definition: very God, Procl.in Prm.p.856S., Eustr.in EN287.34

αὐτόισον.definition: ideal equality, Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.79.14, Procl.in Prm.p.676 S., Herm.in Phdr.p.121A

αὐτόκακον.definition: evil in itself, radical evil; masc. self-tormentor, Theopomp. Com.20

αὐτόκομος.definition: with natural hair, shaggy; leaves and all, Luc.VH1.40

αὐτόκωπος.definition: with haft and blade in one, i.e. swords, A.Ch.163

αὐτομήτωρ.definition: very mother herself, or her mother's very child, dub. in Semon.7.12

αὐτονομία.definition: of a state, freedom to use its own laws; poetic licence, Him.Or.1.1

αὐτόνομος.definition: living under one's own laws; generally, of one's own free will, . . S.Ant.821

αὐτόποκος.definition: made of wool only, all wool, Com.Adesp.854

αὐτόπους.definition: gen. on foot, on one's own feet, Luc.Tim.24

αὐτοτελής.definition: ending in itself, complete in itself; perfect, complete, fully-grown, Nonn.D.7.154,al

αὐτόφυτος.definition: self-engendered: hence, arising; natural, primitive, Arist.Pol.1256a40

αὐτοφωνία.definition: direct utterance, title of work on oracles by Oenomaus, Jul.Or.7.209b

αὐτόφωνος.definition: self-sounding, an oracle delivered by the god himself, Luc.Alex.26

αὐτόφως.definition: very light, Herm.in Phdr.p.118A., cf. Dam.Pr.29, Aen.Gaz.Thphr.p.52B

αὐτόχαρις.definition: very grace: the essence of Attic graces, Alciphr.3.43

αὐτόχροος.definition: contr. with its own; of one and the same colour, ib.330a

αὐτοχωρέω.definition: absorb into oneself, partake of, Anon.in Prm. in Rh.Mus. 47.603

αὐτωνητής.definition: one that buys for himself, Din.Fr.89.11

αὐχενίζω.definition: cut the throat of . . , S.Aj.298; seize by the throat: metaph., Ph.1.654; ib.676:—Pass., 2.372

αὐχένιος.definition: belonging to the neck; stiff-necked, haughty, PMag.Par.1.3058

αὔχημα.definition: thing boasted of, object of pride

αὐχμέω.definition: to be squalid or unwashed, Od.24.250, cf. Ar.Nu.442; to be parched, Pl.R.606d; dry up, Thphr.HP4.10.7:—also part. interpol. in Hp.Prog.2; Arist.Mete.360b11; Thphr.HP8.10.4; Plu.2.187d, Luc.Vit.Auct.7; Id.Apol.6, etc.;…

αὔω.definition: get a light, light a fire, Od.5.490: —Med., take fire, Arat.1035.—Only poet

ἀφαίρεσις.definition: taking away, carrying off, removal; as law-term, assertion of freedom of a reputed slave, Hyp.Fr.23

ἀφαιρέω.definition: Ion. fut. pf. Ion; set aside, SIG 1044.41

ἀφαλμός.definition: springing off, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.31 tit

ἀφαμαρτάνω.definition: aor. part. Orph.A.643; Ep; lose, be deprived of what one has, Il.6.411; 22.505

ἀφανδάνω.definition: Ion. aor. inf. Hdt.2.129:—displease, not to please, Od.16.387; S.Ant.501

ἀφανής.definition: unseen, esp. of the nether; obliterate, SIG38.38

ἀφαρπάζω.definition: fut. Ep. Att. pf. X.Cyn.9.18: aor. 1 Id.HG5.4.17; IPE1.26 : —tear off or from, . . Il.13.189; snatch away, steal from, Ar.Eq.1062: c. acc. only, snatch eagerly, S.Tr.548, E.Ion1178; D.21.64; of death, IG12.52.9 :—Pass…

ἀφαύω.definition: dry up, parch, v.l. for in Ar.Eq.394

ἀφεγγής.definition: without light, a light that is no; not visible to the eye, A.Pr.115

ἀφέτης.definition: one who lets off a military; teacher of ballistic, IG2.465.22

ἀφηλόω.definition: detach, in Pass., Stud.Pal.22.54.16 ; Porph.Abst.1.57:—hence Subst. Gloss

ἀφιδρύω.definition: remove to another settlement, transport, in; make statues or temples after a model, Str.9.2.7, cf. 12.3.32

ἀφιερόω.definition: hallow, consecrate, Ath.3.110b, cf; Pass., I have had these expiatory rites performed, A.Eu.451

ἀφίημι.definition: let fall from one's grasp, Il.12.221; opp. Plu.2.508d; E.Hec.797

ἀφικάνω.definition: Ep. = only pres. and impf., arrive at, mostly c. acc., Od.14.159, al.; . . Il.6.388: c. gen., A.R.1.177

ἀφικνέομαι.definition: Ion. Hdt.2.28, al.: impf; or to try every means, S.OT265, E.Hipp.284; Hdt.8.110; Id.2.28, 77; Gal.2.230

ἀφιλία.definition: want of friends, Arist.EN1115a11, Rh.1386a9, Phld.Oec.p.67J., Plu.Sol.7

ἀφίστημι.definition: cause to revolt, of allies, Id.8.19, Ar.Eq.238, Th.1.81; Hdt.1.76,154, etc.; And.3.22

ἄφολκος.definition: not having weight, too light by a drachm, Str.15.3.22

ἀφοπλίζω.definition: disarm, D.S.11.35, APl.4.171 , Luc.DDeor.19.1:—Pass., D.S.14.64:—Med., put off one's armour, Il.23.26:—Pass. , to be discharged from service, Hsch

ἀφοράω.definition: of Places, look towards, App.Praef.3,cf. Philostr.Im.Prooem; to view from a place, Hdt.4.22; Timocl.21.6

ἀφορίζω.definition: mark off by boundaries; border on, Pl.Criti.110e

ἀφόρισμα.definition: that which is set apart: the wave- offering, LXXEx.29.24, al

ἀφορμάω.definition: intr. in Act. in same sense as Pass., E.Rh.98; Id.Tr.939, cf. Th.4.78; Aeschin.2.40; Plb.1.39.1; of lightning, to break forth, S.OC1470 : c. acc. cogn., . . Id.Aj.290

ἀφοσιόω.definition: Ion. purify from guilt or; dedicate, devote, Clearch.6

ἀφραδέω.definition: only in pres., to be senseless, behave thoughtlessly, . . Il.9.32; Od.7.294

ἀφραίνω.definition: to be foolish, Il.2.258,7.109, Od.20360, Phoc.5.—Poet. and Hp.Gland.12; later as a philosophic term, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.166, Plu.2.1037d, S.E.M.11.94, Plot.5.8.3

ἀφρέω.definition: foam, Hp.Morb.Sacr.7, etc; c. acc., befoam, cover with foam, Il.11.282

ἀφριάω.definition: poet. for Opp.H.1.772, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.11

ἀφρονέω.definition: to be silly, act foolishly; trans., make foolish or vain, f.l. in Aq.2 Ki.15.31

ἀφυβρίζω.definition: work off youthful passion, sow one's wild; of wine, to be done fermenting, Alex.45.4

ἀφύσσω.definition: Ep. impf. Call.Cer.70: fut. Dor; sound, probe, Opp.H.2.597

ἀφύω.definition: to become white or bleached, Hp.Int.40

ἄφωνος.definition: voiceless, dumb, Thgn.669; with a poor voice, D.T.631.21

ἀχάριστος.definition: ungracious, unpleasant; of persons, ungracious, unfavourable, Thgn.841 , Phld.Ir.p.60 W

ἀχεύω.definition: and Ep. Verbs used in pres. part; in causal sense, vex, annoy, redupl. aor. 2 : hence redupl. pres. fut. aor. 1 c. acc. pers., Il.16.822, cf. Od.16.427; ib.432; by his death, Il.23.223; Od.15.357; h.Merc.286

ἄχθομαι.definition: Pass.: fut. Med. Ar.Nu.865,1441, Av.84, Pl.R.603e, Hp.Ma.292e; Pass., And.3.21, Pl.Grg.506c, v.l. in X.Cyr.8.4.10, Aeschin.3.242: pf. Lyc.827: aor. Hdt.2.103, A.Pr.392, Th.6.15, Isoc.12.17:-to be loaded, Od.15.457: c.…

ἀχλυόω.definition: darken, make dim, Aret.CD1.3:—Pass., become gloomy, grow dark, Thphr.Vent.35; become dim, Syn.Alch.p.58B

ἀχλύω.definition: aor. 1 to be or grow dark; trans., darken, Q.S.1.598, Nonn.D.4.368, Pancrat.Oxy.1085.12

ἀχύρωσις.definition: mixing of chaff with mud or straw, compared with the swallow's nest-building, Arist.HA612b22

ἀχωρέω.definition: or suffer from in part. or prob. cj. for in Paul.Aeg.3.3

ἀχώριστος.definition: not parted, undivided; without a place assigned one, X.Lac.9.5

ἀψευδέω.definition: not to lie, to speak truth; observe faithfully, IG5.343.38,57

ἀψευδής.definition: without deceit, truthful, esp. of oracles; of things, uncorrupt, pure from all deceit, Pi.P.1.86

ἁψίκορος.definition: quickly sated: hence, fickle; Act., quickly sating, Plu.2.20b; ib.7b

ἀψίνθιον.definition: wormwood, Artemisia Absinthium; = Artemisia monosperma, Aq.Pr.5.4

ἀψυχία.definition: Ion. swooning, syncope, Id.VM10; want of spirit, faintheartedness, A.Th.259,383, E.Alc.642, etc

ἄω.definition: = , blow, only in impf; = sleep, only in aor., Od.19.342; 3.151; ib.490; contr., 16.367

ἀωροβόρος.definition: devouring those who die untimely, PMag.Par.1.2867

ἀωτέω.definition: sleep, Ep. Verb, only pres., Il.10.159; Od.10.548: abs., Simon.37.5:—in Hsch., , but expld. by AB476, cf. Suid. ; perh. to be read in B.8.13 for

ἀβοηθί.definition: Adv. without assistance, prob. in Euph.54.2

ἀγαμένως.definition: Adv. part. pres. of with admiration or respect, Arist.Rh.1408a18; Pl.Phd.89a

ἁγιώδως.definition: Adv. in sacred manner: Sup. dub. in Ph.1.675

ἀγορῆθεν.definition: Adv.from the assembly or market, Il.2.264, al

ἄγχι.definition: Poet. Adv. of place, near, Il.5.185, Od.3.449; of Time, Sapph.Supp.19.7

ἀγχόθεν.definition: Adv. from near at hand, Hdt.4.31, Luc.Syr.D.28

ἁδόθεν.definition: Adv. from the nether world, Hermesian.7.3

ἀδυσκόλως.definition: Adv. without complaint, prob. in Vit.Philonid.p.13 C

ἀεί.definition: Adv. ever, always, Hom., etc.; with other; Ep., Ion., Poet., and Early Att. ; found in Att. Inscrr. to 361 B.C

ἀερόθεν.definition: Adv. out of the air, from on high, Eust.1239.10

αἰνόθεν.definition: Adv. from only in the phrase horror of horrors, Il.7.97

ἀκᾶ.definition: Dor. Adv. = softly, gently, Pi.P.4.156; cf

ἀκήν.definition: acc. form as Adv., softly, silently, Hom. mostly in phrase Il.3.95, al.; also 4.429

ἀκλητί.definition: Adv. uncalled, unbidden, Com. ap. Zen.2.46 [where

ἀκμήν.definition: acc. of used as Adv., as yet, still; = Cratin.in Cod.Vat.Gr.122: perh., = much, OGI201.13

ἀκμητεί.definition: and Adv. without toil, easily, J.BJ1.16.2, Lib.Or.59.71

ἀκρόθεν.definition: Adv. from the end or top, Arist.Phgn.811a29, Nic.Th.337

ἀκρόθι.definition: Adv. at the end, c. gen., Arat.308

ἀκρονυχί.definition: Adv. with tip of nail, for AP12.126

ἀλλά.definition: Conj., orig. neut. pl. of otherwise: used; in simple oppositions, but

ἄλλοθι.definition: Adv. elsewhere, in another place, esp. in a; in other ways, from other causes, Th.1.16 ; in no other way, Pl.Prt.324e, Smp.184e, etc

ἄλλως.definition: Dor. A.D.Adv.175.13, Adv. of; at all events, any how, . . alone, Id.8.30; . . A.Ch.680

ἅμα.definition: Dor. q.v.: : A. Adv. at once, at the same time, mostly of Time, freq. added to . . Il.8.64; 1.417; 24.773; S.Ph.772, cf. 119; Ant.281:-with only, Il.3.109; with . . Hes.Th.677. 2. . . . . , partly . . partly . . , Pl.…

ἀμάτα.definition: Adv., = SIG421 A5,26 : but perh. cf

ἀμαχητί.definition: Adv. of sq., without battle, without stroke of sword, Il.21.437, Hdt.1.174

ἀμβλήδην.definition: Adv., poet. for :—with sudden bursts, Il.22.476

ἀμβολαδίς.definition: Adv., poet. for either in turns, or with uplifted arms, Call.Dian.61

ἁμῆ.definition: Adv., in a certain way, Hp. ap. Gal.19.78: elsewh. in the phrase somehow or other, Ar.Ach.608, Pl.Prt.331d, R.474c, etc

ἀμοιβαδίς.definition: Adv., by turns, alternately; in turn, again, Epigr.Gr.998.9

ἁμοῦ.definition: Adv. of , somewhere, somewhere or other , Lys.24.20; no-where else at all, IG2.11

ἀμφί.definition: Prep. with gen., dat., acc.: (cf. Skt. abhitas; causal, about, for the sake of, fight for the possession of a spring, Il.16.285; Pi.P.9.105, A.Ag.62; E.Andr.123: like in entreaties, . . for Phoebus' sake, A.R.2.216

ἀμφιπλίξ.definition: Adv. astride: hence, gripping with coils, of serpents, S.Fr.596

ἀμφοτέρῃ.definition: Adv. in both ways, by both branches, of a river, 1.75: Argive Mnemos.47.160

ἀμφουδίς.definition: Adv., only Od.17.237 lifting by the middle

ἁμῶς.definition: or Adv. from obsol. = only in form in some way or other, Ar.Th.429, Lys.13.7, Pl.Prt.323c, Epicur.Fr.607, etc

ἀνά.definition: Aeol., Thess., Arc., Cypr. Prep; of Place, up, from bottom to top, up along, Od.22.176; up to, ib.239; Il.13.547; Hdt.2.96; up-stream, GDI5016.11 ; Ar.Ach.796 ; simply, along, Tab.Heracl.2.32

ἀνάκαρ.definition: Adv., up to or towards the head, upwards, Hp. ap. Gal.19.79

ἀναφανδά.definition: Adv. visibly, openly, before the eyes of all, opp. Od.3.221, 11.455: as neut. Adj., A.R.4.84

ἄνδιχα.definition: Adv., asunder, in twain; as Prep., c. gen., apart from, A.R.1.908, 2.927; AP5.4 :—hence to be divided in opinion, of judges, IG9.333

ἀνέδην.definition: Adv., let loose, freely, without; licentiously, violently, Plb.15.20.3

ἀνειμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of at ease; without accent, opp. Anon.in SE8.23

ἀνέκαθεν.definition: of Time, from the first, being Pylians by origin, Id.5.65, cf. 7.221; more often with the Art., 2.43, cf. 6.128; 5.55, cf. 1.170, 6.35; of ancestral renown, 6.125; OGI566

ἀνεῳγότως.definition: Adv. pf. part. of , openly, Gloss

ἀνηρτημένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of disconnectedly, incoherently, Herm.in Phdr.p.177A

ἀνιδιτί.definition: Adv., without sweat or toil, Pl.Lg.718e

ἀνισάκις.definition: Adv. an unequal number of times, Theo Sm.p.26H., al., Nicom.Ar.2.17

ἄντα.definition: Ep. Adv. over against, face to face, in Hom; as Prep. with gen., like over against, Il.2.626; . . before her cheeks, Od.1.334; 4.115; also of persons, before thee, to thy face, ib.160, cf. 22.232; so in Il.21.331, wit…

ἄντην.definition: Ep. Adv., against, over against; as Prep. c. gen., only in late Ep., as Nic.Th.474, Opp.C.3.210

ἀντί.definition: Prep. governing gen.:—orig. sense, over against; of Place, opposite, over against, formerly quoted from several places of Hom., as Il.21.481 8.233; so 15.415, cf. Od.4.115, Hes.Op.727; but is so used in X.An.4.7.6, IG…

ἀντιπέραν.definition: Ion. Adv. = v.l; Adj., Asia and the opposite coast, Mosch.2.9

ἅπαξ.definition: Adv. once, once only, once for all, first; c. gen., Hdt.2.59, 4.105; also Id.2.132

ἀπαυτίκα.definition: Adv. strengthd. for on the spot, dub. l. in D.C.40.15

ἀπειραχῶς.definition: Adv. in an infinite number of ways, Plu.2.732f, Procl.in Prm.p.581 S

ἀπειροβίως.definition: Adv. without experience of life, Hierocl.p.55 A

ἀπέκ.definition: Prep. with gen., away out of, v.l. in h.Ap.110

ἀπονητί.definition: Adv. of without fatigue, Hdt.3.146, E.Fr.lyr.3, Luc.Rh.Pr.8, al

ἀπονόσφι.definition: before a vowel Ep. Adv. far; c. gen., following its case, far away from, Il.1.541; Od.5.113; ib.12.33

ἀποπρό.definition: Adv. afar off, Il.16.669; as Prep. c. gen., away from, ib.7.334, cf. E.HF1081, Or.142, etc

ἀπρίξ.definition: Adv. fast, tight, S.Aj.310; Subst., a kind of , EM132.53

ἆρα.definition: interrog. Particle, implying anxiety or; alone, it simply marks the question, the nature of which is determined by the context: e.g. in D.35.44 a negative answer is implied in the question . . ; but an affirmative in …

ἄρδην.definition: Adv. contr. for lifted up on

ἁρμοῖ.definition: Adv. just, lately, A.Pr.615, Theoc.4.51; just, a little, ib.4, Steril.213

ἀρχῆθεν.definition: Dor. Adv. from the beginning, from; with neg., . . not at all, Hdt.5.18; cf. I.1 c

ἀστακτί.definition: Adv. of sq., not in drops, i.e. in floods, S. , Pl.Phd.117c

ἄστυδε.definition: Adv. into, to, or towards the city, Il.18.255, Od.17.5, and in late Prose, as Alciphr.1.1

ἄτερ.definition: Ep., Ion., Trag. Prep. with gen., without; aloof, apart from, Il.1.498; Hes.Op.91:—freq. in Trag., mostly after its case, A.Supp.377, etc.; but before it in Id.Pr.456, Supp.703 , Ch.338 , S.Ph.703 , El.866:—also in la…

αὖ.definition: Adv. of repeated action, again, anew, afresh, once; generally, again, i.e. further, moreover, ib.2.493, etc.; Pl.Tht.192b

αὖθι.definition: Adv. shortd. for of Place, on the spot; of Time, forthwith, straightway, Il.5.296, 6.281, etc.— Ep. word, borrowed by S.Fr.522; cf

αὐτοδάξ.definition: Adv. with the very teeth, women angered even to biting, Ar.Lys.687; your ferocious temper, Id.Pax607

αὐτόθι.definition: Adv. = on the spot; later of Time, on the spot, Luc.Cal.24

αὐτολεξεί.definition: Adv. with the very words, in express words, Ph.2.597

αὐτομηνί.definition: Adv. in the very month, Attic. ap. Eus.PE15.4

αὐτονυχί.definition: or Adv., that very; with the nail, EM173.57

αὐτοποδί.definition: Adv. on one's own feet, on foot, D.C.50.5

αὐτοψεί.definition: or Adv. of with one's own eyes, Jul.Ep.204, PSI3.238.11

ἄφαρ.definition: poet. Adv. straightway, forthwith, in Hom; in Thgn.716 as if Adj., swift, fleet

ἄψ.definition: Adv. of Place, backwards, back; of actions, again, in return, Il.22.277; 16.54; 6.427; 9.120; 17.543; 5.505; prob. in Epich.99; = Theoc.25.65: pleon., yet again, Il.8.335, 15.364; 18.280

ἀρετή.definition: ἡ ἀρετή, ἀρετῆς · virtù · valore · eccellenza

ἀρχή.definition: ἡ ἀρχή, ἀρχῆς · inizio · principio · potere · comando
